items.title: Lesson 3: I'm Here!
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 1 级

sents.zh: 我能参观一下录音室吗？

sents.en: Um, maybe another time?
sents.zh: 呃，改天吧？

sents.en: Right now I am busy.
sents.zh: 我现在正忙。

sents.en: Sure.
sents.zh: 好的。

sents.en: Okay, ’bye.
sents.zh: 好，拜拜。

sents.en: ‘Bye.
sents.zh: 拜拜。

sents.en: Hi, Amelia!
sents.zh: 嗨，阿米莉亚！

sents.en: Are you busy?
sents.zh: 你忙吗？

sents.en: I’m a little busy.
sents.zh: 有点忙。

sents.en: I want to say I’m sorry for yesterday.
sents.zh: 我想为昨天的事说声对不起。

sents.en: It’s okay, Anna.
sents.zh: 没关系的，安娜。

sents.en: Well, I am sorry.
sents.zh: 嗯，我还是很抱歉。

sents.en: It’s okay, Anna.
sents.zh: 没关系的，安娜。

sents.en: Come by this afternoon.
sents.zh: 下午过来坐坐吧。

sents.en: Okay.
sents.zh: 好的。

sents.en: Anna.
sents.zh: 安娜。

sents.en: Yes, Ms. Weaver.
sents.zh: 在，韦弗女士。

sents.en: Are you busy?
sents.zh: 你忙吗？

sents.en: Yes, Ms. Weaver.
sents.zh: 是的，韦弗女士。

sents.en: I am busy.
sents.zh: 我在忙。

sents.en: My office.
sents.zh: 来我办公室。

sents.en: Come in.
sents.zh: 进来吧。

sents.en: Surprise!
sents.zh: 惊喜！

sents.en: A party!
sents.zh: 是个派对！

sents.en: Awesome!
sents.zh: 太棒了！

sents.en: And I still have my job!
sents.zh: 而且我的工作还在！

sents.en: Phew!
Until next time!
sents.zh: 下次见！

items.title: Lesson 9: Is It Cold?
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 1 级
items.summaryZh: 安娜问手机天气，却查到了墨西哥城的天气预报。练天气、温度表达。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: VOA Learning English — Let's Learn English

sents.en: Oh, hi, everyone!
sents.zh: 哦，嗨，大家好！

sents.en: Here in Washington, DC, the weather changes often.
sents.zh: 在华盛顿特区，天气变化很快。

sents.en: One day is cold and windy.
sents.zh: 今天还又冷又刮风，

sents.en: But the next day is warm and sunny!
sents.zh: 第二天就暖和又晴朗了！

sents.en: So, every day I check the forecast.
sents.zh: 所以我每天都查天气预报。

sents.en: Hello, Phone?
sents.zh: 喂，手机？

sents.en: What is today’s temperature?
sents.zh: 今天气温多少度？

sents.en: Today it is 18 degrees...
sents.zh: 今天是 18 度……

sents.en: Eighteen degrees!
That is cold!
sents.zh: 好冷啊！

sents.en: … eighteen degrees Celsius.
Oh, Celsius.
sents.zh: 哦，摄氏度啊。

sents.en: That is 65 degrees Fahrenheit.
sents.zh: 那就是华氏 65 度。

sents.en: That’s warm.
sents.zh: 那挺暖和的。

sents.en: Yes, Anna.
sents.zh: 是的，安娜。

sents.en: It is warm.
sents.zh: 天气很暖和。

sents.en: Excuse me, Phone.
sents.zh: 请问，手机，

sents.en: Is it windy today?
sents.zh: 今天刮风吗？

sents.en: No, it is not windy today.
sents.zh: 不，今天不刮风。

sents.en: Is it sunny today?
sents.zh: 今天晴天吗？

sents.en: Yes, Anna.
sents.zh: 是的，安娜。

sents.en: It is sunny.
sents.zh: 今天是晴天。

sents.en: Excuse me, Phone?
sents.zh: 请问，手机？

sents.en: Yes, Anna.
sents.zh: 在，安娜。

sents.en: Is it snowy today?
sents.zh: 今天下雪吗？

sents.en: No, Anna.
sents.zh: 不下，安娜。

sents.en: It is not snowy.
sents.zh: 今天不下雪。

sents.en: Thank you, Phone!
sents.zh: 谢谢你，手机！

sents.en: Today the weather is warm and sunny -- great for seeing Washington, D.C.
sents.zh: 今天天气暖和又晴朗，正适合逛华盛顿！

sents.en: Phone!
sents.zh: 手机！

sents.en: It is not warm and sunny!
sents.zh: 一点都不暖和，也不晴朗！

sents.en: It is cold and windy and snowy!
sents.zh: 又冷、又刮风、还下雪！

sents.en: Anna, it is not cold, windy, or snowy.
sents.zh: 安娜，这里不冷，也不刮风，也不下雪。

sents.en: It is warm and sunny … in Mexico City, Mexico.
sents.zh: 这里暖和又晴朗……墨西哥的墨西哥城。

sents.en: Oh.
sents.zh: 哦。

sents.en: I see.
sents.zh: 明白了。

sents.en: Mexico.
sents.zh: 墨西哥。

sents.en: Washington weather changes often.
sents.zh: 华盛顿的天气变化很快。

sents.en: Remember to check the forecast -- the right forecast.
sents.zh: 记得查天气预报——查对地方的预报。

sents.en: Yes, Anna.
sents.zh: 是的，安娜。

sents.en: Next time remember to check the right fore…
sents.zh: 下次记得查对地方的预……

sents.en: Okay, thank you Phone.
sents.zh: 好啦，谢谢你，手机。

sents.en: Goodbye, Phone.
sents.zh: 再见，手机。

sents.en: Until next time!
sents.zh: 下次见！

items.title: Lesson 10: Come Over to My Place
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 1 级
items.summaryZh: 安娜在电话里给朋友指路：出地铁右拐、到车站左拐、一直走。练问路和指路。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: VOA Learning English — Let's Learn English

sents.en: Hi!
sents.zh: 嗨！

sents.en: Today, my friend Ashley, is coming over.
sents.zh: 今天我的朋友阿什莉要来我家。

sents.en: I am showing her my new apartment!
sents.zh: 我要带她看看我的新公寓！

sents.en: Oh!
sents.zh: 哦！

sents.en: That’s Ashley calling.
sents.zh: 是阿什莉打来的。

sents.en: Hi Ashley!
sents.zh: 嗨，阿什莉！

sents.en: Hi Anna!
sents.zh: 嗨，安娜！

sents.en: I’m coming to your apartment.
sents.zh: 我正往你公寓去。

sents.en: Where is your apartment?
sents.zh: 你的公寓在哪儿？

sents.en: My apartment is near the Columbia Heights Metro.
sents.zh: 我的公寓在哥伦比亚高地地铁站附近。

sents.en: It is near the Columbia Heights Metro?
sents.zh: 在哥伦比亚高地地铁站附近？

sents.en: Yes.
sents.zh: 对。

sents.en: Exit the Metro and turn right.
sents.zh: 出了地铁站往右拐。

sents.en: Then at the bus station turn left.
sents.zh: 然后到公交车站往左拐。

sents.en: Then walk straight ahead.
sents.zh: 然后一直往前走。

sents.en: Okay.
sents.zh: 好的。

sents.en: Exit Metro, turn right, turn left, then go straight ahead?
sents.zh: 出地铁，右拐，左拐，然后直走？

sents.en: Yes.
sents.zh: 对。

sents.en: My apartment is near a coffee shop.
sents.zh: 我的公寓在一家咖啡店附近。

sents.en: Okay.
sents.zh: 好的。

sents.en: See you soon!
sents.zh: 一会儿见！

sents.en: Hi, Ashley.
sents.zh: 嗨，阿什莉。

sents.en: Anna, Which coffee shop?
sents.zh: 安娜，哪家咖啡店啊？

sents.en: There are three coffee shops.
sents.zh: 这里有三家咖啡店。

sents.en: Okay, my apartment is across from a big department store.
sents.zh: 好吧，我的公寓在一家大百货商店对面。

sents.en: A big department store?
sents.zh: 大百货商店？

sents.en: Ah, I see it!
sents.zh: 啊，我看到了！

sents.en: Okay!
sents.zh: 好！

sents.en: Bye, Ashley.
sents.zh: 拜拜，阿什莉。

sents.en: See you soon!
sents.zh: 一会儿见！

sents.en: Okay.
sents.zh: 好的。

sents.en: See you soon.
sents.zh: 一会儿见。

sents.en: Ashley!
sents.zh: 阿什莉！

sents.en: Ashley!
sents.zh: 阿什莉！

sents.en: Ashley!
sents.zh: 阿什莉！

sents.en: Over here!
sents.zh: 这边！

sents.en: It’s Anna!
sents.zh: 是我，安娜！

sents.en: It’s Anna!
sents.zh: 是我，安娜！

sents.en: Hi!
sents.zh: 嗨！

sents.en: I love having my friends over.
sents.zh: 我很喜欢请朋友来家里玩。

sents.en: Come on!
sents.zh: 快进来！

sents.en: Great!
sents.zh: 好啊！

items.title: Lesson 11: This Is My Neighborhood
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 1 级
items.summaryZh: 在家附近办杂事：图书馆还书、寄信、银行取钱、买邮票，最后吃冰淇淋。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: VOA Learning English — Let's Learn English

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 大家好！

sents.en: DC is a city for walking.
sents.zh: 华盛顿是一座适合步行的城市。

sents.en: In our neighborhood, I can do all my errands.
sents.zh: 在我们街区，各种杂事走路都能办完。

sents.en: Marsha, before we get ice cream, I need to return three books to the library.
sents.zh: 玛莎，买冰淇淋之前，我得先去图书馆还三本书。

sents.en: Where is the library?
sents.zh: 图书馆在哪儿？

sents.en: It is on this street on the corner.
sents.zh: 就在这条街的街角。

sents.en: Awesome!
sents.zh: 太棒了！

sents.en: Let's go!
sents.zh: 走吧！

sents.en: Marsha, I can return the books here.
sents.zh: 玛莎，书可以在这里还。

sents.en: Anna, what are those in the books?
sents.zh: 安娜，书里夹的那些是什么？

sents.en: Marsha, these are letters to my family and friends back home … four letters!
sents.zh: 玛莎，这些是给家乡亲友写的信……四封！

sents.en: Is there a post office near here?
sents.zh: 这附近有邮局吗？

sents.en: Um, no.
sents.zh: 呃，没有。

sents.en: The post office is far from here.
sents.zh: 邮局离这儿很远。

sents.en: But there is a mailbox across from the store.
sents.zh: 不过商店对面有个邮筒。

sents.en: Awesome!
sents.zh: 太棒了！

sents.en: Let’s go!
sents.zh: 走吧！

sents.en: Marsha, now I need to buy stamps.
sents.zh: 玛莎，现在我得买邮票。

sents.en: Do you have cash?
sents.zh: 你有现金吗？

sents.en: No. Is there a bank near here?
sents.zh: 没有。这附近有银行吗？

sents.en: There is a bank behind you.
sents.zh: 你身后就是一家银行。

sents.en: Thanks, Marsha.
sents.zh: 谢谢你，玛莎。

sents.en: You know our neighborhood so well.
sents.zh: 你对我们这片真熟。

sents.en: Now I have cash.
sents.zh: 现在我有现金了。

sents.en: I can buy stamps.
sents.zh: 可以买邮票了。

sents.en: That store sells stamps.
sents.zh: 那家店卖邮票。

sents.en: Wait here.
sents.zh: 在这儿等我一下。

sents.en: I have stamps.
sents.zh: 邮票买好了。

sents.en: Wow, you’re fast.
sents.zh: 哇，你真快。

sents.en: Thank you, thank you letters, for sending my words… my love … to my family and friends -
sents.zh: 谢谢你们，信啊，替我把我的话……我的爱……带给我的家人和朋友——

sents.en: Do you have more cash?
sents.zh: 你还有现金吗？

sents.en: I do!
sents.zh: 有啊！

sents.en: Ice cream!!
sents.zh: 冰淇淋！！

sents.en: I love my new neighborhood!
sents.zh: 我爱我的新街区！

sents.en: Everything is near our apartment!
sents.zh: 什么都离我们公寓很近！

sents.en: Even hair salons, and ice cream!
sents.zh: 连美发店和冰淇淋店都有！

sents.en: Until next time!
sents.zh: 下次见！

items.title: Lesson 12: Meet My Family
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 1 级
items.summaryZh: 安娜想家，给室友看全家福：父母、姨妈、叔叔、堂兄妹。练家庭成员称呼。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: VOA Learning English — Let's Learn English

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 大家好！

sents.en: Washington, D.C. has many beautiful parks.
sents.zh: 华盛顿特区有很多漂亮的公园。

sents.en: In fact, this park reminds me of my home very far away.
sents.zh: 其实，这个公园让我想起了远方的家。

sents.en: Anna, here's your coffee.
sents.zh: 安娜，你的咖啡。

sents.en: Thanks, Marsha.
sents.zh: 谢谢你，玛莎。

sents.en: What's wrong?
sents.zh: 怎么了？

sents.en: I'm thinking about my family.
sents.zh: 我在想我的家人。

sents.en: I'm feeling homesick.
sents.zh: 我有点想家。

sents.en: Do you want to talk about it?
sents.zh: 想聊聊吗？

sents.en: Sure!
sents.zh: 好啊！

sents.en: I have some photos.
sents.zh: 我带了些照片。

sents.en: Yes.
sents.zh: 嗯。

sents.en: Yes, you do!
sents.zh: 嗯，你确实带了不少！

sents.en: Photos really help.
sents.zh: 看看照片真的有用。

sents.en: This is my mother and this is my father.
sents.zh: 这是我妈妈，这是我爸爸。

sents.en: They are rodeo clowns.
sents.zh: 他们是牛仔竞技表演里的小丑。

sents.en: What do rodeo clowns do?
sents.zh: 竞技小丑是做什么的？

sents.en: They make jokes at a rodeo.
sents.zh: 他们在牛仔竞技场上逗乐子。

sents.en: They make people laugh.
sents.zh: 他们逗大家笑。

sents.en: That… That's very different.
sents.zh: 那……那可真特别。

sents.en: Who is that woman in the picture?
sents.zh: 照片里那位女士是谁？

sents.en: That is my Aunt Lavender.
sents.zh: 那是我的拉文德姨妈。

sents.en: She is my mom's sister.
sents.zh: 她是我妈妈的妹妹。

sents.en: She loves gardening and makes spoons.
sents.zh: 她喜欢园艺，还会做勺子。

sents.en: She makes spoons?
sents.zh: 她做勺子？

sents.en: Of course.
sents.zh: 当然啦。

sents.en: That, too, is very different.
sents.zh: 那也挺特别的。

sents.en: Oh!
sents.zh: 哦！

sents.en: This is my Uncle John.
sents.zh: 这是我的约翰叔叔。

sents.en: He is my father's brother.
sents.zh: 他是我爸爸的弟弟。

sents.en: What does Uncle John do?
sents.zh: 约翰叔叔是做什么的？

sents.en: He's a chicken farmer.
sents.zh: 他养鸡。

sents.en: And makes guitars.
sents.zh: 还做吉他。

sents.en: He's awesome, and I'm his favorite niece.
sents.zh: 他超棒的，我是他最喜欢的侄女。

sents.en: Who are they?
sents.zh: 他们是谁？

sents.en: They are my cousins.
sents.zh: 他们是我的堂兄妹。

sents.en: They are my Uncle John's daughter and son.
sents.zh: 是约翰叔叔的女儿和儿子。

sents.en: What do they do?
sents.zh: 他们做什么？

sents.en: They raise sheep and make sweaters.
sents.zh: 他们养羊，织毛衣。

sents.en: Yeah, that's not a surprise.
sents.zh: 嗯，这一点也不意外。

sents.en: Thanks for showing me your family photos.
sents.zh: 谢谢你给我看你的家庭照片。

sents.en: Your family is very different.
sents.zh: 你的家人真的很特别。

sents.en: I do feel better.
sents.zh: 我确实感觉好多了。

sents.en: Thanks for listening.
sents.zh: 谢谢你听我说。

sents.en: I have many more photos!
sents.zh: 我还有好多照片呢！

sents.en: Yeah.
sents.zh: 嗯。

sents.en: Yeah, you do.
sents.zh: 嗯，看得出来。

sents.en: Washington, DC is my new home.
sents.zh: 华盛顿是我的新家。

sents.en: But I like remembering my old home, too.
sents.zh: 不过我也喜欢回忆我原来的家。

items.title: Lesson 14: How About This?
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 1 级
items.summaryZh: 晚上要去剧院，安娜不知道穿什么，杂志里的“精灵”帮她挑衣服。练衣服、尺码、颜色。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: VOA Learning English — Let's Learn English

sents.en: Hi, there!
sents.zh: 嗨，大家好！

sents.en: In Washington, D.C. people do many things in the evening.
sents.zh: 在华盛顿，人们晚上会做很多事。

sents.en: They go listen to music.
sents.zh: 他们去听音乐，

sents.en: They eat at a restaurant.
sents.zh: 去餐馆吃饭，

sents.en: They go to the theater.
sents.zh: 去剧院看戏。

sents.en: Tonight I am going to the theater with my friends.
sents.zh: 今晚我要和朋友们去剧院。

sents.en: But I don’t know what clothes to wear.
sents.zh: 可是我不知道该穿什么衣服。

sents.en: Maybe this magazine can help.
sents.zh: 也许这本杂志能帮上忙。

sents.en: Her clothes are beautiful!
sents.zh: 她的衣服真漂亮！

sents.en: I really want a friend like her to help me.
sents.zh: 我真想有个像她这样的朋友来帮我。

sents.en: Who are you?
sents.zh: 你是谁？

sents.en: I am Genie!
sents.zh: 我是精灵！

sents.en: You want help.
sents.zh: 你需要帮忙。

sents.en: I am here to help you find the right clothes!
sents.zh: 我来帮你挑合适的衣服！

sents.en: Awesome!
sents.zh: 太棒了！

sents.en: How about jeans and a t-shirt?
sents.zh: 牛仔裤配 T 恤怎么样？

sents.en: No!
sents.zh: 不行！

sents.en: Jeans and a t-shirt are too casual.
sents.zh: 牛仔裤配 T 恤太随便了。

sents.en: How about something more formal?
sents.zh: 来点正式一些的怎么样？

sents.en: Sure!
sents.zh: 好啊！

sents.en: Wow!
sents.zh: 哇！

sents.en: Genie, this dress is beautiful.
sents.zh: 精灵，这条裙子真漂亮。

sents.en: But it’s not the right size.
sents.zh: 可是尺码不对。

sents.en: It’s too small.
sents.zh: 太小了。

sents.en: Yes, it is too small.
sents.zh: 是啊，太小了。

sents.en: But green looks great on you.
sents.zh: 不过你穿绿色很好看。

sents.en: Thanks.
sents.zh: 谢谢。

sents.en: Take off the green dress.
sents.zh: 把绿裙子脱了吧。

sents.en: Let’s try a green shirt and a skirt.
sents.zh: 我们试试绿衬衫配半身裙。

sents.en: Oh, Genie!
sents.zh: 哦，精灵！

sents.en: This green shirt is too large and this orange skirt is too orange.
sents.zh: 这件绿衬衫太大了，这条橙色裙子也太橙了。

sents.en: Yes, the right size for you is medium.
sents.zh: 是啊，你适合中号。

sents.en: Let’s try again.
sents.zh: 再试一次。

sents.en: Oh, I don’t like this outfit.
sents.zh: 哦，我不喜欢这身搭配。

sents.en: No. That does not match.
sents.zh: 是啊，这样不搭。

sents.en: Nothing.
sents.zh: 什么都不对。

sents.en: These clothes are formal: a suit jacket, a dress shirt and a tie!
sents.zh: 这身衣服很正式：西装外套、正装衬衫，还有领带！

sents.en: They look great!
sents.zh: 看起来很棒！

sents.en: Those clothes look great … for a man!
sents.zh: 这身衣服是很好看……穿在男人身上！

sents.en: Something is wrong.
sents.zh: 有点不对劲。

sents.en: Let me see.
sents.zh: 让我看看。

sents.en: There.
sents.zh: 好了。

sents.en: Now try.
sents.zh: 现在你来试。

sents.en: Oh.
sents.zh: 哦。

sents.en: Thanks!
sents.zh: 谢谢！

sents.en: Now these clothes look great on you!
sents.zh: 这下这身衣服你穿着真好看！

sents.en: They do!
sents.zh: 确实！

sents.en: Um, Genie, can you put on a gold belt?
sents.zh: 呃，精灵，你能系一条金色腰带吗？

sents.en: Sure!
sents.zh: 当然！

sents.en: That looks great.
sents.zh: 好看。

sents.en: Can you put on a jacket?
sents.zh: 能穿件外套吗？

sents.en: Why not?
sents.zh: 有何不可？

sents.en: I love the jacket!
sents.zh: 我好喜欢这件外套！

sents.en: How about a hat?
sents.zh: 再戴顶帽子怎么样？

sents.en: Why not?
sents.zh: 有何不可？

sents.en: Mm, take off the hat.
sents.zh: 嗯，帽子还是摘了吧。

sents.en: That’s better.
sents.zh: 这样好多了。

sents.en: Genie, these clothes look and feel great!
sents.zh: 精灵，这身衣服好看又舒服！

sents.en: Let’s go to the theater!
sents.zh: 我们去剧院吧！

sents.en: Sorry, Anna.
sents.zh: 抱歉，安娜。

sents.en: I have to help other friends.
sents.zh: 我得去帮其他朋友了。

sents.en: Go to the magazine if you want me to help again.
sents.zh: 想让我再帮忙，就去翻那本杂志。

sents.en: Thanks, Genie.
sents.zh: 谢谢你，精灵。

sents.en: Sure thing.
sents.zh: 没问题。

sents.en: Goodbye!
sents.zh: 再见！

sents.en: Goodbye!
sents.zh: 再见！

sents.en: There are many places in DC to go for a great evening out!
sents.zh: 华盛顿有很多适合晚上出去玩的地方！

sents.en: And it’s nice to have a friend to help me look my best.
sents.zh: 有个朋友帮我打扮得漂漂亮亮的，真好。

sents.en: Until next time!
sents.zh: 下次见！

sents.en: Bye!
sents.zh: 拜拜！

items.title: Lesson 15: I Love People-Watching!
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 1 级
items.summaryZh: 午休时在户外看路人，描述外貌：高矮、眼睛、头发、肤色，没想到老板来了。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: VOA Learning English — Let's Learn English

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 大家好！

sents.en: People from all over the world come to Washington, D.C. When I’m at work, I love eating lunch outside.
sents.zh: 世界各地的人都会来华盛顿。上班的时候，我喜欢在外面吃午饭。

sents.en: I like to watch people walking by.
sents.zh: 我喜欢看路过的行人。

sents.en: They all look very different.
sents.zh: 他们每个人看起来都很不一样。

sents.en: Today, my friend Ashley is eating lunch with me.
sents.zh: 今天我的朋友阿什莉和我一起吃午饭。

sents.en: Ashley, today the weather is beautiful, isn’t it?
sents.zh: 阿什莉，今天天气真好，是吧？

sents.en: Yes, it is.
sents.zh: 是啊。

sents.en: Ahh.
Ooh, we have to return to work!
sents.zh: 噢，我们得回去上班了！

sents.en: No, we have time!
sents.zh: 不，还有时间呢！

sents.en: Let’s people-watch a little more.
sents.zh: 我们再看会儿人吧。

sents.en: Okay.
sents.zh: 好吧。

sents.en: Oh, I know her.
sents.zh: 哦，我认识她。

sents.en: She works in my office!
sents.zh: 她在我们办公室上班！

sents.en: Keyana, hi!
sents.zh: 基亚娜，嗨！

sents.en: Come and join us!
sents.zh: 过来一起坐吧！

sents.en: Hi Anna, how are you?
sents.zh: 嗨，安娜，你好吗？

sents.en: I’m doing great!
sents.zh: 我很好！

sents.en: Keyana, this is my friend Ashley.
sents.zh: 基亚娜，这是我的朋友阿什莉。

sents.en: Hi, Ashley!
sents.zh: 嗨，阿什莉！

sents.en: We need to return to work.
sents.zh: 我们得回去上班了。

sents.en: But the weather is beautiful and people-watching is fun!
sents.zh: 可是天气这么好，看人又很有意思！

sents.en: I love people-watching too!
sents.zh: 我也喜欢看人！

sents.en: Well, have a seat!
sents.zh: 那就坐吧！

sents.en: It is fun to see how people are different or the same.
sents.zh: 看看人和人哪里不同、哪里相同，挺有意思的。

sents.en: It is.
sents.zh: 是啊。

sents.en: For example, Anna, you are tall.
sents.zh: 比如说，安娜，你个子高。

sents.en: But Ashley and I are short.
sents.zh: 可是阿什莉和我个子矮。

sents.en: And Keyana, you and Ashley have brown eyes; I have blue eyes.
sents.zh: 还有基亚娜，你和阿什莉是棕色眼睛，我是蓝眼睛。

sents.en: You two have light skin and I have dark skin.
sents.zh: 你们俩皮肤白，我皮肤黑。

sents.en: Ashley, you have straight hair.
sents.zh: 阿什莉，你是直发。

sents.en: Keyana and I have curly hair.
sents.zh: 基亚娜和我是卷发。

sents.en: You have very curly hair, Anna.
sents.zh: 安娜，你的头发卷得厉害。

sents.en: I need to return to work.
sents.zh: 我得回去上班了。

sents.en: See you, Anna!
sents.zh: 回头见，安娜！

sents.en: Nice to meet you Ashley!
sents.zh: 很高兴认识你，阿什莉！

sents.en: Bye, Keyana!
sents.zh: 拜拜，基亚娜！

sents.en: Anna, I have to go, too.
sents.zh: 安娜，我也得走了。

sents.en: Are you returning to work?
sents.zh: 你回去上班吗？

sents.en: I still have time.
sents.zh: 我还有时间。

sents.en: And this sun feels so good!
sents.zh: 这太阳晒着太舒服了！

sents.en: Um, Anna, what does your boss look like?
sents.zh: 呃，安娜，你的上司长什么样？

sents.en: She is short.
sents.zh: 她个子矮。

sents.en: She has straight, light hair.
sents.zh: 一头浅色直发。

sents.en: Does she wear glasses?
sents.zh: 她戴眼镜吗？

sents.en: Yes.
sents.zh: 戴。

sents.en: Yes, she does.
sents.zh: 对，她戴眼镜。

sents.en: Is she wearing a blue sweater today?
sents.zh: 她今天是不是穿着一件蓝毛衣？

sents.en: How do you know that?
sents.zh: 你怎么知道？

sents.en: She’s coming this way.
sents.zh: 她正往这边走呢。

sents.en: Oh no!
sents.zh: 哦，不！

sents.en: Hide me!
sents.zh: 快把我藏起来！

sents.en: Um, bye, Anna.
sents.zh: 呃，拜拜，安娜。

sents.en: Call me later.
sents.zh: 回头给我打电话。

sents.en: Bye, Ashley!
sents.zh: 拜拜，阿什莉！

sents.en: Talk to you later!
sents.zh: 回头聊！

sents.en: Anna?
sents.zh: 安娜？

sents.en: Is that you?
sents.zh: 是你吗？

sents.en: Ms. Weaver!
sents.zh: 韦弗女士！

sents.en: Hi!
sents.zh: 嗨！

sents.en: What are you doing behind that bench?
sents.zh: 你躲在长椅后面干什么？

sents.en: I am looking for my, my … stick.
sents.zh: 我在找我的……我的……棍子。

sents.en: Here it is.
sents.zh: 找到了。

sents.en: I am people-watching.
sents.zh: 我在看人。

sents.en: Oh!
sents.zh: 哦！

sents.en: But it’s time to return to work!
sents.zh: 不过该回去上班了！

sents.en: No need to hurry.
sents.zh: 不用急。

sents.en: I love people-watching too!
sents.zh: 我也喜欢看人！

sents.en: Let’s sit!
sents.zh: 坐会儿吧！

sents.en: Sure!
sents.zh: 好啊！

sents.en: Ahh.
It’s a beautiful day, isn’t it?
sents.zh: 今天天气真好，是吧？

sents.en: Yes.
sents.zh: 是啊。

sents.en: Yes, it is, Ms. Weaver.
sents.zh: 是啊，韦弗女士。

sents.en: People-watching in D.C. is fun.
sents.zh: 在华盛顿看人真有意思。

sents.en: It makes me forget the time!
sents.zh: 让我都忘了时间！

sents.en: Until next time!
sents.zh: 下次见！

sents.en: Ahh.

items.title: Lesson 16: Where Are You From?
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 1 级
items.summaryZh: 安娜在华盛顿采访各国游客：国籍、语言、喜欢做什么。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: VOA Learning English — Let's Learn English

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 大家好！

sents.en: Washington, D.C. has many tourists!
sents.zh: 华盛顿有很多游客！

sents.en: People from different countries come here.
sents.zh: 不同国家的人都来这里。

sents.en: Today, my job is to interview tourists.
sents.zh: 今天我的任务是采访游客。

sents.en: I have to learn why they come here.
sents.zh: 我要了解他们为什么来这里。

sents.en: This is very exciting!
sents.zh: 真让人兴奋！

sents.en: Excuse me.
sents.zh: 打扰一下。

sents.en: I’m Anna Matteo from The News.
sents.zh: 我是《新闻》的安娜·马泰奥。

sents.en: Do you have time for an interview?
sents.zh: 您有时间接受一下采访吗？

sents.en: Sure, I have time.
sents.zh: 当然，我有时间。

sents.en: What is your name?
sents.zh: 您叫什么名字？

sents.en: My name is Sabrina.
sents.zh: 我叫萨布丽娜。

sents.en: What country are you from?
sents.zh: 您来自哪个国家？

sents.en: I’m from Bangladesh.
sents.zh: 我来自孟加拉国。

sents.en: So, you are Bangladeshi.
sents.zh: 那您是孟加拉人。

sents.en: That’s right!
sents.zh: 没错！

sents.en: My nationality is Bangladeshi.
sents.zh: 我的国籍是孟加拉。

sents.en: Do you like Washington, D.C.?
sents.zh: 您喜欢华盛顿吗？

sents.en: Yes!
sents.zh: 喜欢！

sents.en: The city is very beautiful!
sents.zh: 这座城市很美！

sents.en: What do you like to do in Washington D.C.?
sents.zh: 您在华盛顿喜欢做什么？

sents.en: I like history.
sents.zh: 我喜欢历史。

sents.en: So, I like walking around and looking at all the monuments and memorials.
sents.zh: 所以我喜欢四处走走，看看各种纪念碑和纪念馆。

sents.en: They make history come alive!
sents.zh: 它们让历史变得鲜活起来！

sents.en: Washington has many monuments and memorials.
sents.zh: 华盛顿有很多纪念碑和纪念馆。

sents.en: The Washington Monument is behind us!
sents.zh: 华盛顿纪念碑就在我们身后！

sents.en: Which is your favorite?
sents.zh: 您最喜欢哪一个？

sents.en: I really like Lincoln Memorial.
sents.zh: 我特别喜欢林肯纪念堂。

sents.en: It is very beautiful.
sents.zh: 它非常漂亮。

sents.en: And it feels like Abraham Lincoln is still alive.
sents.zh: 感觉亚伯拉罕·林肯好像还活着。

sents.en: Awesome.
sents.zh: 太好了。

sents.en: Thank you for your time, Sabrina!
sents.zh: 谢谢您抽出时间，萨布丽娜！

sents.en: You’re welcome.
sents.zh: 不客气。

sents.en: Let’s find another tourist.
sents.zh: 我们再找一位游客。

sents.en: Oh!
sents.zh: 哦！

sents.en: Excuse me.
sents.zh: 打扰一下。

sents.en: I am Anna Matteo from The News.
sents.zh: 我是《新闻》的安娜·马泰奥。

sents.en: Do you have time for a couple of questions?
sents.zh: 您有时间回答几个问题吗？

sents.en: Sure!
sents.zh: 当然！

sents.en: Are you from Washington, D.C.?
sents.zh: 您是华盛顿本地人吗？

sents.en: No, I’m not.
sents.zh: 不，我不是。

sents.en: What is your name and where are you from?
sents.zh: 您叫什么名字？从哪里来？

sents.en: My name is Louis.
sents.zh: 我叫路易斯。

sents.en: And I’m from China.
sents.zh: 我来自中国。

sents.en: What languages do you speak?
sents.zh: 您会说哪些语言？

sents.en: I speak Chinese and English.
sents.zh: 我会说中文和英语。

sents.en: What do you like about Washington DC?
sents.zh: 您喜欢华盛顿的什么？

sents.en: I like the museums.
sents.zh: 我喜欢这里的博物馆。

sents.en: I really like the art museums.
sents.zh: 我特别喜欢美术馆。

sents.en: Many of the museums are free.
sents.zh: 很多博物馆都是免费的。

sents.en: I like that too!
sents.zh: 这一点我也喜欢！

sents.en: Awesome!
sents.zh: 太好了！

sents.en: Thanks for your time, Louis.
sents.zh: 谢谢您抽出时间，路易斯。

sents.en: You’re very welcome.
sents.zh: 非常乐意。

sents.en: Bye!
sents.zh: 再见！

sents.en: Now, let’s find another tourist!
sents.zh: 好，我们再找一位游客！

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 您好！

sents.en: I am Anna Matteo from The News.
sents.zh: 我是《新闻》的安娜·马泰奥。

sents.en: Do you have time to answer a couple of questions?
sents.zh: 您有时间回答几个问题吗？

sents.en: Sure!
sents.zh: 当然！

sents.en: What is your name and where’re you from?
sents.zh: 您叫什么名字？从哪里来？

sents.en: My name is Mehrnoush.
sents.zh: 我叫梅赫努什。

sents.en: I am from Iran.
sents.zh: 我来自伊朗。

sents.en: I’m Iranian.
sents.zh: 我是伊朗人。

sents.en: What language do they speak in Iran?
sents.zh: 伊朗人说什么语言？

sents.en: Is it Persian?
sents.zh: 是波斯语吗？

sents.en: They speak Farsi.
sents.zh: 他们说法尔西语。

sents.en: What do you like to do in Washington DC?
sents.zh: 您在华盛顿喜欢做什么？

sents.en: Well, I like learning about government and politics.
sents.zh: 嗯，我喜欢了解政府和政治。

sents.en: Washington has many politicians!
sents.zh: 华盛顿的政治人物可多了！

sents.en: It does!
sents.zh: 确实！

sents.en: I want to see the U.S. Capitol.
sents.zh: 我想去看看美国国会大厦。

sents.en: Look, you are very near.
sents.zh: 看，您离它很近了。

sents.en: I am!
sents.zh: 真的！

sents.en: Have fun!
sents.zh: 玩得开心！

sents.en: Thanks!
sents.zh: 谢谢！

sents.en: There you have it.
sents.zh: 就是这样。

sents.en: Tourists from all over the world come to Washington, D.C. They all like doing and seeing different things in the city.
sents.zh: 世界各地的游客都会来华盛顿。他们在这座城市里喜欢做的事、想看的东西各不相同。

sents.en: This is Anna Matteo reporting for The News.
sents.zh: 这里是《新闻》的安娜·马泰奥为您报道。

sents.en: Until next time!
sents.zh: 下次见！

sents.en: Is that okay?
sents.zh: 这样可以吗？

sents.en: Awesome!
sents.zh: 太棒了！

sents.en: Now, I want to do my favorite thing in the city … ride the carousel!
sents.zh: 现在我要去做我在这座城市最喜欢的事……坐旋转木马！

items.title: Lesson 1: Budget Cuts
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 2 级
items.summaryZh: 公司要开重要会议，大家听到“预算削减”的传言都担心被裁员，结果虚惊一场。练职场词汇。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: VOA Learning English — Let's Learn English

sents.en: Hum.
sents.zh: 嗯。

sents.en: Oh!
sents.zh: 哦！

sents.en: “Important meeting.
sents.zh: “重要会议。

sents.en: Everyone must come.”
sents.zh: 全员参加。”

sents.en: Well, back to work!
sents.zh: 好吧，继续工作！

sents.en: And my boss has called a meeting.
sents.zh: 我的上司召集了一个会。

sents.en: I wonder what it's about.
sents.zh: 不知道是关于什么的。

sents.en: Maybe we're all getting raises!
sents.zh: 说不定大家都要涨工资了！

sents.en: Ooo, there's Jonathan!
sents.zh: 哦，乔纳森来了！

sents.en: Maybe he knows.
sents.zh: 也许他知道。

sents.en: Hi!
sents.zh: 嗨！

sents.en: I'm Professor Bot!
sents.zh: 我是机器人教授！

sents.en: This video is all about work.
sents.zh: 这一集讲的全是工作。

sents.en: People talk about jobs and things that happen at work.
sents.zh: 大家会聊各种职业，还有工作中发生的事。

sents.en: Your assignment is to find as many work words as you can.
sents.zh: 你的任务是尽可能多地找出和工作有关的词。

sents.en: Don't worry, I'll help.
sents.zh: 别担心，我会帮你。

sents.en: So, Jonathan, what do you think today's meeting is about?
sents.zh: 乔纳森，你觉得今天的会是关于什么的？

sents.en: The email sounded important.
sents.zh: 那封邮件听起来很重要。

sents.en: Well, I have heard people in the building talking about budget cuts.
sents.zh: 嗯，我听楼里的人在议论预算削减。

sents.en: Oh!
sents.zh: 哦！

sents.en: Budget cuts?
sents.zh: 预算削减？

sents.en: Wait, who has been talking about budget cuts?
sents.zh: 等等，是谁在议论预算削减？

sents.en: Mark in Accounting.
sents.zh: 会计部的马克。

sents.en: Mark in Accounting?
sents.zh: 会计部的马克？

sents.en: That's one person.
sents.zh: 那只是一个人。

sents.en: That's not “people.”
sents.zh: 不能算“大家”。

sents.en: I know, but Mark knows everything that goes on at The Studio.
sents.zh: 我知道，可马克对工作室里发生的事无所不知。

sents.en: That is true.
sents.zh: 这倒是真的。

sents.en: But wait, look at us.
sents.zh: 等等，看看我们俩。

sents.en: We shouldn't gossip.
sents.zh: 我们不该嚼舌根。

sents.en: That's how rumors start.
sents.zh: 谣言就是这么来的。

sents.en: We'll just go to the meeting and see what happens.
sents.zh: 我们就去开会，看看会怎么样。

sents.en: You're right.
sents.zh: 你说得对。

sents.en: No more talk about budget cuts.
sents.zh: 不再谈预算削减了。

sents.en: Budget cuts?
sents.zh: 预算削减？

sents.en: Oh no!
sents.zh: 哦，不！

sents.en: I just heard Anna and Jonathan talking about budget cuts.
sents.zh: 我刚听到安娜和乔纳森在说预算削减。

sents.en: That must be what the meeting is about.
sents.zh: 今天开会肯定就是为这事。

sents.en: When there are budget cuts, people lose their jobs.
sents.zh: 一削减预算，就会有人丢工作。

sents.en: Not you.
sents.zh: 不会是你。

sents.en: You're a good reporter.
sents.zh: 你是个好记者。

sents.en: And it's not you.
sents.zh: 也不会是你。

sents.en: You've done a great job as a videographer.
sents.zh: 你当摄像师一直干得很好。

sents.en: I can't go back to being a detective.
sents.zh: 我可不能回去当侦探了。

sents.en: Criminals scare me!
sents.zh: 罪犯太吓人了！

sents.en: And I can't go back to being a teacher!
sents.zh: 我也不能回去当老师了！

sents.en: High school kids scare me!
sents.zh: 高中生太吓人了！

sents.en: Did you hear any work words?
sents.zh: 你听到和工作有关的词了吗？

sents.en: They talked about a lot of jobs.
sents.zh: 他们聊到了很多职业。

sents.en: You can make the name of a job by adding an ending to a verb!
sents.zh: 在动词后面加个词尾，就能变成职业名称！

sents.en: Kaveh reports, so, he's a reporter.
sents.zh: 卡维做报道，所以他是记者（reporter）。

sents.en: Amelia used to detect, so she was a detective.
sents.zh: 阿米莉亚以前做侦查，所以她当过侦探（detective）。

sents.en: If you teach, you're a teacher.
sents.zh: 你教书，就是老师（teacher）。

sents.en: And a videographer….uh, I think you understand.
sents.zh: 还有摄像师……呃，我想你明白了。

sents.en: Back to the story.
sents.zh: 回到故事。

sents.en: Penelope, have you heard the news?
sents.zh: 佩内洛普，你听说了吗？

sents.en: Today's meeting is about budget cuts.
sents.zh: 今天的会是关于预算削减的。

sents.en: That's awful!
sents.zh: 太可怕了！

sents.en: What should I do?
sents.zh: 我该怎么办？

sents.en: Update your résumé.
sents.zh: 更新一下你的简历吧。

sents.en: I’ve already updated mine.
sents.zh: 我已经更新好了。

sents.en: I’ll see you at the meeting.
sents.zh: 会上见。

sents.en: Hello everyone!
sents.zh: 大家好！

sents.en: Quiet, please.
sents.zh: 请安静。

sents.en: Quiet, please!
sents.zh: 请安静！

sents.en: This meeting won’t take long.
sents.zh: 这个会不会开很久。

sents.en: Then you can all leave.
sents.zh: 开完大家就可以走了。

sents.en: What is wrong with everyone?
sents.zh: 大家这是怎么了？

sents.en: You look like I'm going to fire you.
sents.zh: 一个个看起来像是我要开除你们似的。

sents.en: Ha-ha-ha-ha-ha!
sents.zh: 哈哈哈哈哈！

sents.en: Seriously, what is wrong with everyone?
sents.zh: 说真的，大家怎么了？

sents.en: Excuse me, Ms. Weaver?
sents.zh: 打扰一下，韦弗女士？

sents.en: Yes, Anna.
sents.zh: 什么事，安娜。

sents.en: Well, everyone has been worrying about, you know …
sents.zh: 嗯，大家一直在担心，您知道的……

sents.en: We’ve been worrying that you are going to fire us!
sents.zh: 我们一直担心您要开除我们！

sents.en: I’m not going to fire any of you!
sents.zh: 我谁也不会开除！

sents.en: No!
sents.zh: 不会的！

sents.en: The reason for this meeting is to tell you what a good job you’ve been doing and give out new assignments.
sents.zh: 开这个会是想告诉大家你们干得有多好，再给大家分配新任务。

sents.en: Budget cuts have been happening.
sents.zh: 预算确实一直在削减。

sents.en: But only one person has lost their job -- Mark in Accounting?
sents.zh: 不过只有一个人丢了工作——会计部的马克？

sents.en: Now, let’s talk about those new assignments.
sents.zh: 好，我们来说说新任务。

sents.en: Ms. Weaver's team is doing a good job!
sents.zh: 韦弗女士的团队干得不错！

sents.en: How did you do?
sents.zh: 你做得怎么样？

sents.en: Did you find all of the work words?
sents.zh: 和工作有关的词都找到了吗？

sents.en: Here's a list you can check.
sents.zh: 这里有一份清单，你可以对一对。

items.title: Lesson 2: The Interview
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 2 级
items.summaryZh: 老板给安娜派新任务：找一个和她性格相反的人搭档主持节目，安娜推荐了皮特去面试。练短语动词。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: VOA Learning English — Let's Learn English

sents.en: Ms. Weaver is giving new assignments out.
sents.zh: 韦弗女士正在分配新任务。

sents.en: I am ready to take on anything she gives me.
sents.zh: 不管她给我什么任务，我都准备好接了。

sents.en: Well, except reporting traffic from a helicopter.
sents.zh: 嗯，除了坐直升机报道路况。

sents.en: Wish me luck.
sents.zh: 祝我好运吧。

sents.en: I wonder what Anna’s new assignment will be?
sents.zh: 不知道安娜的新任务会是什么？

sents.en: Professor Bot here!
sents.zh: 我是机器人教授！

sents.en: While you are watching, look for phrasal, or two-word verbs.
sents.zh: 看的时候，留意一下短语动词，也就是两个词组成的动词。

sents.en: Some stay together, like “go back” and some can come apart, like “give [assignments] out.”
sents.zh: 有些是连在一起用的，比如 go back；有些可以拆开，比如 give [assignments] out。

sents.en: Good luck, Anna!
sents.zh: 祝你好运，安娜！

sents.en: So, as I said at the meeting last week, I have new assignments for everyone at The Studio.
sents.zh: 就像我上周开会时说的，我给工作室的每个人都安排了新任务。

sents.en: Anna, you're good at asking questions.
sents.zh: 安娜，你很会提问。

sents.en: So, I want you to go back to hosting and reporting.
sents.zh: 所以我想让你回去做主持和报道。

sents.en: That sounds great.
sents.zh: 听起来很棒。

sents.en: You're also a team player.
sents.zh: 你也很有团队精神。

sents.en: So, I want you team up with someone...
sents.zh: 所以我想让你和一个人搭档……

sents.en: That sounds even better!
sents.zh: 那听起来更好了！

sents.en: ... someone who is very "different" from you.
sents.zh: ……一个和你非常“不一样”的人。

sents.en: That sounds... what do you mean "different"?
sents.zh: 听起来……您说的“不一样”是什么意思？

sents.en: Well, you are very cheerful, you're a people person.
sents.zh: 嗯，你性格很开朗，很会和人打交道。

sents.en: I want you to team up with someone who... isn't.
sents.zh: 我想让你和一个……不是这样的人搭档。

sents.en: Ms. Weaver, I will find that person.
sents.zh: 韦弗女士，我会找到这个人的。

sents.en: Excuse me.
sents.zh: 打扰一下。

sents.en: Are you using this chair?
sents.zh: 这把椅子有人坐吗？

sents.en: Yes.
sents.zh: 有。

sents.en: Pete, hi!
sents.zh: 皮特，嗨！

sents.en: Thanks for meeting me.
sents.zh: 谢谢你出来见我。

sents.en: Sure.
sents.zh: 没事。

sents.en: But I don’t have lots of time, Anna.
sents.zh: 不过我时间不多，安娜。

sents.en: I’m busy looking for work.
sents.zh: 我正忙着找工作。

sents.en: Pete, you can tear these want ads up and throw them away!
sents.zh: 皮特，这些招聘广告你可以撕了扔掉了！

sents.en: I have good news!
sents.zh: 我有好消息！

sents.en: Anna, I was working on that crossword puzzle.
sents.zh: 安娜，我刚才在做那个填字游戏。

sents.en: Oh.
sents.zh: 哦。

sents.en: Sorry.
sents.zh: 对不起。

sents.en: Sorry.
sents.zh: 对不起。

sents.en: Pete, forget about the crossword puzzle.
sents.zh: 皮特，别管填字游戏了。

sents.en: I have a job offer for you!
sents.zh: 我给你带来了一个工作机会！

sents.en: I'm listening.
sents.zh: 你说，我听着。

sents.en: My boss wants me to team up with someone to host a talk show.
sents.zh: 我的上司想让我和一个人搭档主持一档谈话节目。

sents.en: But the person must be different from me.
sents.zh: 但这个人得和我不一样。

sents.en: So, I thought of you.
sents.zh: 所以我想到了你。

sents.en: Different from you?
sents.zh: 和你不一样？

sents.en: What do you mean?
sents.zh: 什么意思？

sents.en: I'm sorry, Pete, I don't have time right now.
sents.zh: 对不起，皮特，我现在没时间了。

sents.en: Here's my boss's address.
sents.zh: 这是我上司的地址。

sents.en: Your interview is tomorrow morning at 10 am.
sents.zh: 你的面试是明天上午十点。

sents.en: But what do you mean “different”?
sents.zh: 可你说的“不一样”到底是什么意思？

sents.en: Just be yourself, Pete.
sents.zh: 做你自己就好，皮特。

sents.en: Just be yourself.
sents.zh: 做你自己就好。

sents.en: Did you find any two-word verbs?
sents.zh: 你找到两个词组成的动词了吗？

sents.en: Here’s one example.
sents.zh: 举个例子。

sents.en: Pete can throw the want ads away!
sents.zh: 皮特可以把招聘广告扔掉（throw away）！

sents.en: Throw away is a two-word verb.
sents.zh: throw away 就是一个两个词的动词。

sents.en: Thanks for coming in, Pete.
sents.zh: 谢谢你过来，皮特。

sents.en: Thanks for the opportunity, Ms. Weaver.
sents.zh: 谢谢您给我这个机会，韦弗女士。

sents.en: I need to find out if you have the skills for this job.
sents.zh: 我需要了解你有没有做这份工作的能力。

sents.en: And I want you to be completely honest.
sents.zh: 我希望你完全实话实说。

sents.en: Okay.
sents.zh: 好的。

sents.en: First, let's talk about your personal skills.
sents.zh: 首先，我们聊聊你的个人能力。

sents.en: Pete, are you a people person?
sents.zh: 皮特，你擅长和人打交道吗？

sents.en: Well, okay, sometimes I think people talk too much.
sents.zh: 嗯，好吧，有时候我觉得人们话太多了。

sents.en: Pete, what work of yours are you most proud of?
sents.zh: 皮特，你最自豪的作品是什么？

sents.en: Last year, I locked myself in a cabin and wrote a book.
sents.zh: 去年我把自己关在一间小木屋里写了一本书。

sents.en: I didn't speak to anybody the entire time!
sents.zh: 整个期间我没跟任何人说过话！

sents.en: It was the best two months of my life.
sents.zh: 那是我人生中最美好的两个月。

sents.en: Okay.
sents.zh: 好的。

sents.en: I think I’ve heard enough.
sents.zh: 我想我听得差不多了。

sents.en: Hey!
sents.zh: 嘿！

sents.en: Hey, Pete, how was the interview with Ms. Weaver?
sents.zh: 嘿，皮特，和韦弗女士的面试怎么样？

sents.en: Well, she said I was grumpy and not good with people.
sents.zh: 嗯，她说我脾气暴躁，不会和人相处。

sents.en: And …?
sents.zh: 然后呢……？

sents.en: And, I got the job!
sents.zh: 然后，我被录用了！

sents.en: I knew it!
sents.zh: 我就知道！

sents.en: Congratulations!
sents.zh: 恭喜！

sents.en: Let's go celebrate.
sents.zh: 我们去庆祝一下吧。

sents.en: Okay!
sents.zh: 好！

sents.en: Did you find more two-word verbs?
sents.zh: 你找到更多两个词的动词了吗？

sents.en: Here is the list.
sents.zh: 清单在这里。

items.title: Lesson 5: Greatest Vacation of All Time
items.series: Let's Learn English 第 2 级
items.summaryZh: 安娜去旅行社挑度假套餐，推销员一个比一个贵。练比较级和最高级、交通方式。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: VOA Learning English — Let's Learn English

sents.en: “Do you need a vacation?”
sents.zh: “你需要一个假期吗？”

sents.en: Wow.
sents.zh: 哇。

sents.en: That was the best vacation I have ever had … in my head.
sents.zh: 那是我度过的最棒的假期……在我脑子里。

sents.en: A beach is much better than here.
sents.zh: 海滩可比这儿好多了。

sents.en: I need a vacation!
sents.zh: 我需要休个假！

sents.en: I hear you, Anna.
sents.zh: 我懂你，安娜。

sents.en: I need a vacation too but not at the beach.
sents.zh: 我也需要休假，但不去海滩。

sents.en: Sand is not good for robots!
sents.zh: 沙子对机器人可不好！

sents.en: When we compare things, we use special forms of adjectives.
sents.zh: 比较事物的时候，我们会用形容词的特殊形式。

sents.en: "Better" is a comparative adjective.
sents.zh: better 是形容词的比较级。

sents.en: That is used to compare two things.
sents.zh: 用来比较两样东西。

sents.en: "Best" is a superlative adjective.
sents.zh: best 是形容词的最高级。

sents.en: It shows that one thing has more of...something than ALL of the others.
sents.zh: 它表示某样东西在某方面比其他所有的都更……

sents.en: Try to find more of these adjectives.
sents.zh: 试着多找几个这样的形容词。

sents.en: Look for ER or EST at the end.
sents.zh: 留意结尾的 -er 和 -est。

sents.en: NO!
sents.zh: 不行！

sents.en: You can’t get your money back.
sents.zh: 钱不能退给你。

sents.en: I don’t care that it was your worst vacation ever!
sents.zh: 我才不管那是不是你最糟糕的一次假期！

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 您好！

sents.en: Have a seat!
sents.zh: 请坐！

sents.en: Welcome to the World’s Best Vacation Travel Agency!
sents.zh: 欢迎来到全球最佳度假旅行社！

sents.en: Thank you and congratulations!
sents.zh: 谢谢，也恭喜你们！

sents.en: For what?
sents.zh: 恭喜什么？

sents.en: For being the world’s best travel agency.
sents.zh: 恭喜你们成为全球最佳旅行社。

sents.en: Right … thanks.
sents.zh: 对……谢谢。

sents.en: Trudy, hold my calls.
sents.zh: 特鲁迪，电话先帮我挡一下。

sents.en: I am going to sell our most expensive vacation.
sents.zh: 我要卖出我们最贵的度假套餐。

sents.en: Sure thing, Boss.
sents.zh: 没问题，老板。

sents.en: The Mountain Getaway is good for you.
sents.zh: “高山度假”挺适合您。

sents.en: It’s a little pricey.
sents.zh: 价格稍微有点贵。

sents.en: But think of it -- you, on top of a mountain for seven days!
sents.zh: 不过想想看——您在山顶待上七天！

sents.en: I’m afraid of high places.
sents.zh: 我恐高。

sents.en: Of course you are.
sents.zh: 当然啦。

sents.en: That’s why our Deep Sea Adventure is better for you!
sents.zh: 所以我们的“深海探险”更适合您！

sents.en: It is pricier than the Mountain Getaway.
sents.zh: 它比“高山度假”还贵一些。

sents.en: Just you and the animals of the sea!
sents.zh: 只有您和海洋动物！

sents.en: Shark!
sents.zh: 鲨鱼！

sents.en: Shark!
sents.zh: 鲨鱼！

sents.en: No, there are no sharks in your dream vacation!
sents.zh: 不不，您梦想中的假期里没有鲨鱼！

sents.en: You need the Safari Camp Out!
sents.zh: 您需要的是“野生动物营地露营”！

sents.en: It is our priciest vacation.
sents.zh: 这是我们最贵的套餐。

sents.en: But I think it’s the best one for you.
sents.zh: 但我觉得这是最适合您的。

sents.en: During the day, you’ll see elephants, giraffes and lions.
sents.zh: 白天您能看到大象、长颈鹿和狮子。

sents.en: At night, you’ll sleep out under the stars.
sents.zh: 晚上您就睡在星空下。

sents.en: Look, I think this was a bad idea.
sents.zh: 呃，我觉得这是个馊主意。

sents.en: Sure, you can leave.
sents.zh: 当然，您可以走。

sents.en: But then you won’t see the latest vacation technology.
sents.zh: 不过那样您就看不到最新的度假科技了。

sents.en: Did you find all of those adjectives?
sents.zh: 这些形容词你都找到了吗？

sents.en: Dan started with good - The mountain getaway; then he moved to better - The Deep Sea Adventure.
sents.zh: 丹先说“好”——高山度假；然后升级到“更好”——深海探险。

sents.en: And finally, he said the Safari Campout was the best vacation for Anna!
sents.zh: 最后他说野生动物营地露营是最适合安娜的假期！

sents.en: Exactly what is the “latest vacation technology” … exactly?
sents.zh: 所谓“最新的度假科技”……到底是什么？

sents.en: I’m happy you asked.
sents.zh: 很高兴您问了。

sents.en: Meet the Travel Max 2000!
sents.zh: 来认识一下“旅行大师 2000”！

sents.en: Wow.
sents.zh: 哇。

sents.en: So, tell me, how do you like to travel?
sents.zh: 那么告诉我，您喜欢怎么旅行？

sents.en: Well, I like travel that is cozy and romantic but still exciting.
sents.zh: 嗯，我喜欢舒适、浪漫但又刺激的旅行。

sents.en: Great.
sents.zh: 很好。

sents.en: Tell me more.
sents.zh: 再多说一点。

sents.en: I like traveling in a plane but not in a helicopter!
sents.zh: 我喜欢坐飞机，但不坐直升机！

sents.en: Planes are a little scary but helicopters are scarier!
sents.zh: 飞机有点吓人，直升机更吓人！

sents.en: My favorite way of traveling is by train.
sents.zh: 我最喜欢的出行方式是坐火车。

sents.en: Ships can be the scariest!
sents.zh: 坐船可能最吓人！

sents.en: Have you seen the movie “Titanic”?
sents.zh: 您看过电影《泰坦尼克号》吗？

sents.en: Oh, and no horses.
sents.zh: 哦，还有，不要骑马。

sents.en: But I will ride a camel.
sents.zh: 不过骆驼我可以骑。

sents.en: And no bike tours.
sents.zh: 也不要骑车游。

sents.en: Biking is THE slowest AND least romantic way to travel.
sents.zh: 骑自行车是最慢、也最不浪漫的旅行方式。

sents.en: Excuse me, but I think the Travel Max 2000 is on fire.
sents.zh: 不好意思，我觉得“旅行大师 2000”着火了。

sents.en: Yes, we’re both on fire!
sents.zh: 是啊，我们俩都火力全开！

sents.en: We really want to sell you the most ex-, I mean, best vacation ever!
sents.zh: 我们真的很想卖给您最贵——我是说，最棒的假期！

sents.en: No, I mean it’s really on fire!
sents.zh: 不，我是说它真的着火了！

sents.en: You killed it.
sents.zh: 你把它弄坏了。

sents.en: You killed the Travel Max 2000!
sents.zh: 你把“旅行大师 2000”弄坏了！

sents.en: I am so sorry!
sents.zh: 真对不起！

sents.en: Can I help you fix it?
sents.zh: 要我帮你修吗？

sents.en: No, no!
sents.zh: 不，不用！

sents.en: Don’t cry.
sents.zh: 别哭啊。

sents.en: I know what you need -- a vacation!
sents.zh: 我知道你需要什么——一个假期！

sents.en: The Safari Campout looks fun.
sents.zh: “野生动物营地露营”看起来很好玩。

sents.en: It is the priciest.
sents.zh: 它是最贵的。

sents.en: But I think you deserve it.
sents.zh: 不过我觉得你值得。

sents.en: No, no!
sents.zh: 不，不要！

sents.en: Oh Anna.
sents.zh: 哦，安娜。

sents.en: This is the smokiest lesson yet!
sents.zh: 这是到目前为止烟最大的一课！

sents.en: There were a lot of comparatives and superlatives but …
sents.zh: 这一课有很多比较级和最高级，可是……

sents.en: I can’t breathe.
sents.zh: 我喘不过气了。

sents.en: Just go to the website to learn the best ways to use them!
sents.zh: 去网站上学学它们的最佳用法吧！

items.title: Speaking Fluently
items.series: Ask a Teacher 问问老师
items.summaryZh: 老师回答：流利不等于不犯错，而是不怎么停顿、能聊很多话题。需要大量词汇和表达，再加上大量开口练习。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Andrew Smith wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English.

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 大家好！

sents.en: This week on Ask a Teacher, we answer a question from Aaron Ali in Sudan about how to become a fluent speaker.
sents.zh: 本周的《问问老师》，我们来回答苏丹的阿龙·阿里提的问题：怎样才能说一口流利的英语。

sents.en: Dear Teacher,
sents.zh: 亲爱的老师：

sents.en: I have been learning English since 2010, but I can't speak English fluently, even now.
sents.zh: 我从 2010 年开始学英语，可是到现在还是说不流利。

sents.en: Could you tell me how to get my English fluent?
sents.zh: 您能告诉我怎样让英语变流利吗？

sents.en: Thank you for writing to us, Aaron Ali.
sents.zh: 谢谢你的来信，阿龙·阿里。

sents.en: I’m happy to answer this question.
sents.zh: 我很乐意回答这个问题。

sents.en: To help you reach your goal, consider the following two questions:
sents.zh: 为了帮你达到目标，先想想下面两个问题：
第一，

sents.en: What is making it difficult for you to become fluent?
sents.zh: 是什么让你很难说得流利？
第二，

sents.en: Are you getting the input and practice with English that you need?
sents.zh: 你在英语上得到的输入和练习够不够？

sents.en: Input means the language you listen to and read.
sents.zh: 输入指的是你听到和读到的语言。

sents.en: Being fluent does not mean speaking a language without any mistakes.
sents.zh: 流利并不是说一门语言时一点错误都没有。

sents.en: Instead, fluency is the ability to speak without stopping too much.
sents.zh: 流利指的是说话时不会频繁停顿。

sents.en: It is also the ability to speak about a large number of issues.
sents.zh: 也指能谈论很多不同的话题。

sents.en: Try to identify what is preventing you from being fluent.
sents.zh: 试着找出是什么在妨碍你说流利。

sents.en: Maybe you worry about making grammar mistakes.
sents.zh: 也许你担心犯语法错误。

sents.en: Maybe pronunciation problems slow you down.
sents.zh: 也许发音问题让你说得慢。

sents.en: Perhaps you simply might not know enough words.
sents.zh: 也许只是你会的词还不够多。

sents.en: Or, you might need more confidence, or belief in yourself.
sents.zh: 又或者，你需要更多信心，也就是相信自己。

sents.en: If that is the case, our VOA Learning English article linked here gives advice for gaining more confidence in your speaking.
sents.zh: 如果是这样，这里链接的这篇 VOA 慢速英语文章，给出了怎样在说英语时更有信心的建议。

sents.en: People generally need two things to become fluent.
sents.zh: 一般来说，想说流利需要两样东西。

sents.en: The first thing they need is to know a lot of words and expressions.
sents.zh: 第一，要掌握大量的单词和表达。

sents.en: You should listen to and read English that you can mostly understand but that also helps you learn a few new expressions at a time.
sents.zh: 你应该多听、多读那些大部分能看懂、同时又能让你一次学到几个新表达的英语。

sents.en: Remember, you can be fluent even if you make many grammar mistakes.
sents.zh: 记住，即使语法错误很多，你也可以说得很流利。

sents.en: But you cannot speak fluently if you do not know enough words and expressions.
sents.zh: 但如果单词和表达不够，你就没法说流利。

sents.en: The second thing learners need is a lot of practice speaking in different kinds of situations.
sents.zh: 第二，学习者需要在各种不同场合大量练习说。

sents.en: Try to find an English-speaking partner and practice often.
sents.zh: 试着找一个说英语的语伴，经常练习。

sents.en: Online sites can help you find a language partner.
sents.zh: 一些网站可以帮你找到语伴。

sents.en: You can have a conversation with this person over a mobile phone or computer.
sents.zh: 你们可以用手机或电脑聊天。

sents.en: And this VOA Learning English article gives advice for great language exchanges.
sents.zh: 这篇 VOA 慢速英语文章还介绍了怎样做好语言交换。

sents.en: Practice speaking about particular topics.
sents.zh: 围绕特定话题练习说。

sents.en: For example, if you are interested in health and exercise, learn the words and expressions connected to that topic.
sents.zh: 比如，如果你对健康和运动感兴趣，就去学和这个话题相关的单词和表达。

sents.en: Next, try to write about it.
sents.zh: 接着，试着写一写这个话题。

sents.en: Writing can help you organize your ideas and remember vocabulary.
sents.zh: 写作能帮你整理思路、记住词汇。

sents.en: Last, practice speaking about the topic, using the special vocabulary you have learned.
sents.zh: 最后，用学到的专门词汇练习说这个话题。

sents.en: Storytelling is another way to practice.
sents.zh: 讲故事是另一种练习方法。

sents.en: It helps you learn expressions and grammatical forms.
sents.zh: 它能帮你学会各种表达和语法形式。

sents.en: Tell a story many times.
sents.zh: 把一个故事讲很多遍。

sents.en: That will help you feel what it is like to speak fluently.
sents.zh: 这能让你体会到说得流利是什么感觉。

sents.en: Reading out loud is another way to practice, and the video and article linked here gives advice about doing that.
sents.zh: 大声朗读也是一种练习方法，这里链接的视频和文章介绍了具体做法。

sents.en: Finally, our How to Pronounce series shows you how to say common phrases quickly and easily.
sents.zh: 最后，我们的《怎么读》系列会教你怎样又快又轻松地说常用短语。

sents.en: For our readers and listeners, do you have a question about American English?
sents.zh: 各位读者和听众，你有关于美国英语的问题吗？

sents.en: Send us an email at learningenglish@voanews.com.
sents.zh: 请发邮件到 learningenglish@voanews.com。

sents.en: And that’s Ask a Teacher.
sents.zh: 以上就是本期《问问老师》。

sents.en: I’m Andrew Smith.
sents.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。

items.title: Thinking in English
items.series: Ask a Teacher 问问老师
items.summaryZh: 为什么第二次聊天比第一次流利？因为要用的词和语法已经练熟了。提前想好话题、练到自动化。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Andrew Smith wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English.

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 大家好！

sents.en: This week on Ask a Teacher, we answer a question from Hoang in Vietnam about how to think in English.
sents.zh: 本周的《问问老师》，我们来回答越南的黄提的问题：怎样用英语思考。

sents.en: Dear Teacher,
sents.zh: 亲爱的老师：

sents.en: People say that to speak English fluently, you need to think in English.
sents.zh: 人们说，想把英语说流利，就得用英语思考。

sents.en: So how can I think in English faster?
sents.zh: 那我怎样才能更快地用英语思考呢？

sents.en: When I talk with foreigners…with the first conversation, I talk very slowly and the remaining time I use for thinking.
sents.zh: 我和外国人聊天时……第一轮对话我说得很慢，剩下的时间都在想。

sents.en: And with the second conversation (because I've been talking before), I feel natural and I speak more fluently.
sents.zh: 到第二轮对话（因为之前已经聊过了），我就觉得很自然，也说得更流利。

sents.en: So how can I be fluent like the second conversation when I'm having the first conversation?
sents.zh: 那我怎样才能在第一轮对话时就像第二轮那样流利呢？

sents.en: Thank you,
sents.zh: 谢谢您，

sents.en: Hoang
sents.zh: 黄

sents.en: I’m happy to answer this question, Hoang.
sents.zh: 我很乐意回答这个问题，黄。

sents.en: It can be difficult to fully explain how to think in a foreign language.
sents.zh: 要完整解释怎样用外语思考，可能有点难。

sents.en: That is because the explanation asks us to consider the relationship between thoughts and the language we use to express them.
sents.zh: 因为这需要我们去思考：想法和我们用来表达想法的语言之间是什么关系。

sents.en: However, we can still notice what happens when we think in a foreign language.
sents.zh: 不过，我们还是可以观察用外语思考时会发生什么。

sents.en: And we can compare it to times when we have to pause and translate from our native language.
sents.zh: 也可以把它和我们必须停下来从母语翻译的时候做个比较。

sents.en: Consider what happens when you exchange simple greetings, questions, and answers in a foreign language.
sents.zh: 想想你用外语互相打招呼、简单问答时是什么情况。

sents.en: If someone asks you in English, “How are you today?” you can probably answer without pausing or translating from your native language.
sents.zh: 如果有人用英语问你 “How are you today?”，你大概不用停顿、也不用从母语翻译就能回答。

sents.en: For example, you can quickly reply, “I’m fine, thank you.
sents.zh: 比如，你可以马上回答：“I’m fine, thank you.

sents.en: And how are you?”
sents.zh: And how are you?”

sents.en: This example shows us the basic things we need for thinking in a foreign language.
sents.zh: 这个例子告诉我们，用外语思考需要哪些基本条件。

sents.en: In this situation, you know all the words you need to say.
sents.zh: 在这种情况下，你要说的词你全都会。

sents.en: You don’t need to stop and think about the grammar.
sents.zh: 你不需要停下来想语法。

sents.en: And you have heard and said these phrases so many times that your response is automatic.
sents.zh: 而且这些话你听过、说过太多遍了，回答已经是自动的。

sents.en: The reason the second conversation you talk about feels more natural is because you have already heard and used some of the vocabulary and grammar you need.
sents.zh: 你说的第二轮对话之所以感觉更自然，是因为你已经听过、用过一些需要的词汇和语法。

sents.en: So, for any subject you want to discuss, you will be able to think in English after you have learned and practiced what you need to say many times.
sents.zh: 所以，不管你想谈什么话题，只要把要说的内容学会、练过很多遍，你就能用英语思考了。

sents.en: Here are some suggestions for learning to think in English:
sents.zh: 下面是学习用英语思考的一些建议：

sents.en: Choose a subject you are interested in discussing.
sents.zh: 选一个你有兴趣讨论的话题。

sents.en: Then, imagine you are speaking with another person.
sents.zh: 然后，想象你正在和另一个人说话。

sents.en: How easily and quickly can your mind find the vocabulary and grammar you need?
sents.zh: 你的大脑能多轻松、多快地找到需要的词汇和语法？

sents.en: Note when you need to pause to find vocabulary or think about grammar.
sents.zh: 留意你在什么时候需要停下来找词或想语法。

sents.en: Next, learn the vocabulary and grammar and then practice using them several times.
sents.zh: 接着，把这些词汇和语法学会，再练习用几遍。

sents.en: Repeat the words until they become automatic.
sents.zh: 反复说这些词，直到它们变成自动反应。

sents.en: If you can plan ahead and practice in your mind what you will likely talk about, then your first conversation might feel easier and similar to a second conversation.
sents.zh: 如果你能提前计划，在脑子里先练练可能会聊的内容，那第一轮对话可能就会轻松一些，像第二轮一样。

sents.en: You can find more advice for thinking in English in our Education Tips article, “Train Your Brain to Think in English.”
sents.zh: 更多用英语思考的建议，可以看我们《学习技巧》栏目的文章《训练大脑用英语思考》。

sents.en: Keep in mind that, to think in English, you need to read, listen to, and speak as much English as possible.
sents.zh: 记住，想用英语思考，就要尽可能多地读、听、说英语。

sents.en: This will help your mind use English more easily.
sents.zh: 这会让你的大脑更自如地使用英语。

sents.en: For our readers and listeners, what are your questions about American English?
sents.zh: 各位读者和听众，你们有什么关于美国英语的问题吗？

sents.en: We’d like to hear from you.
sents.zh: 我们很想听到你们的声音。

sents.en: Send us an email at learningenglish@voanews.com.
sents.zh: 请发邮件到 learningenglish@voanews.com。

sents.en: And please include where you are from in your email, too.
sents.zh: 也请在邮件里写上你来自哪里。

sents.en: And that’s Ask a Teacher.
sents.zh: 以上就是本期《问问老师》。

sents.en: I’m Andrew Smith.
sents.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。

items.title: Practice Your Listening
items.series: Ask a Teacher 问问老师
items.summaryZh: 反复听不等于背录音：选稍难一点的材料，先盲听抓大意，再看文字核对；听写、变速、听不同口音。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Andrew Smith wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English.

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 大家好！

sents.en: This week on Ask a Teacher, we answer a question from Zekeriya in Turkiye about listening to English.
sents.zh: 本周的《问问老师》，我们来回答土耳其的泽凯里亚关于英语听力的问题。

sents.en: Dear teacher,
sents.zh: 亲爱的老师：

sents.en: When I practice listening, I focus a lot and do a lot of repetitions.
sents.zh: 我练听力时非常专注，会反复听很多遍。

sents.en: After a while, I realized that I was actually memorizing the audio recording instead of practicing listening.
sents.zh: 过了一段时间，我发现自己其实是在背录音，而不是在练听力。

sents.en: How do you think I should do an ideal listening exercise?
sents.zh: 您觉得理想的听力练习应该怎么做？

sents.en: Thank you,
sents.zh: 谢谢您，

sents.en: I’m happy to answer this question, Zekeriya.
sents.zh: 我很乐意回答这个问题，泽凯里亚。

sents.en: There is not one ideal listening exercise.
sents.zh: 并没有哪一种练习是唯一理想的听力练习。

sents.en: Instead, there are several good ways to improve your listening.
sents.zh: 但有好几种不错的方法可以提高听力。

sents.en: The repetitions you are doing can be necessary and helpful for you to understand what you hear.
sents.zh: 你现在做的反复听，对于听懂内容来说可能是必要的，也很有帮助。

sents.en: And repetitions likely help you remember new words and how to pronounce them.
sents.zh: 反复听也很可能帮你记住新单词和它们的读音。

sents.en: But let’s look at more ways you can practice listening.
sents.zh: 不过我们再看看还有哪些练听力的方法。

sents.en: First, try to find listening material that is just a bit above your ability.
sents.zh: 首先，尽量找比你现有水平稍微高一点的听力材料。

sents.en: This will help you learn new words without making it too difficult for you.
sents.zh: 这样既能学到新词，又不会难得让你吃不消。

sents.en: It is best to listen to English material that has words written either in captions or in the body text, such as a VOA Learning English article.
sents.zh: 最好听那种配有文字的英语材料，文字可以是字幕，也可以是正文，比如 VOA 慢速英语的文章。

sents.en: This will help check your listening.
sents.zh: 这样可以检查你听得对不对。

sents.en: You can test yourself by first listening to parts of the audio without reading the words.
sents.zh: 你可以先不看文字，听其中几段来测试自己。

sents.en: Note the main ideas and the things you clearly understood.
sents.zh: 记下主要意思，以及你清楚听懂的内容。

sents.en: Then, listen to it again and try to understand more details.
sents.zh: 然后再听一遍，试着听懂更多细节。

sents.en: This is when you can do shorter repetitions.
sents.zh: 这时候可以分成更短的片段反复听。

sents.en: Next, you can check how much you understood by reading the words as you listen to the audio again.
sents.zh: 接下来，你可以一边再听音频一边看文字，检查自己听懂了多少。

sents.en: One of the best ways to practice listening is by writing every word you hear.
sents.zh: 练听力最好的方法之一，就是把听到的每个词都写下来。

sents.en: This is called transcribing.
sents.zh: 这叫作听写。

sents.en: Even with audio examples as short as one minute, you can learn a lot of English using this method.
sents.zh: 即使音频只有一分钟这么短，用这个方法也能学到很多英语。

sents.en: For example, if you are transcribing an interview, you might notice differences between spoken English and written English.
sents.zh: 比如，听写一段采访时，你可能会注意到口语英语和书面英语的区别。

sents.en: By transcribing, you can notice and learn new expressions, grammar rules and spelling.
sents.zh: 通过听写，你能注意到并学会新的表达、语法规则和拼写。

sents.en: This method also helps make new words stay in your memory when you read them.
sents.zh: 这个方法还能让你在读到新词时记得更牢。

sents.en: That is because you are discovering the answer to a problem you have already tried to solve through listening.
sents.zh: 因为你是在为一个已经试着靠听力去解决的问题找答案。

sents.en: Try listening to English spoken at different speeds.
sents.zh: 试着听不同语速的英语。

sents.en: Over time, you can follow spoken English at a faster speed.
sents.zh: 慢慢地，你就能跟上更快的英语了。

sents.en: Many videos online let you increase or decrease the speed of playback.
sents.zh: 网上很多视频都可以调快或调慢播放速度。

sents.en: Practice listening to English spoken in different foreign accents.
sents.zh: 练习听带有各种外国口音的英语。

sents.en: This is a useful skill because English is spoken in so many places around the world.
sents.zh: 这项能力很有用，因为世界上很多地方都说英语。

sents.en: Center your listening on specific sounds or grammatical points.
sents.zh: 把听的重点放在某些特定的发音或语法点上。

sents.en: For example, preposition use in English can be difficult.
sents.zh: 比如，英语介词的用法可能很难。

sents.en: Try listening for prepositions and the words they connect with.
sents.zh: 试着专门去听介词，以及和它们搭配的词。

sents.en: This can help you use them correctly in your speaking and writing.
sents.zh: 这能帮你在说和写的时候正确使用介词。

sents.en: Remember that, like any skill, you can improve listening by practicing often and having detailed plans for the methods you will use.
sents.zh: 记住，和任何技能一样，只要经常练习、对要用的方法有详细计划，听力就能提高。

sents.en: For our readers and listeners, what are your questions about American English?
sents.zh: 各位读者和听众，你们有什么关于美国英语的问题吗？

sents.en: We’d like to hear from you.
sents.zh: 我们很想听到你们的声音。

sents.en: Send us an email at learningenglish@voanews.com.
sents.zh: 请发邮件到 learningenglish@voanews.com。

sents.en: And please include where you are from in your email, too.
sents.zh: 也请在邮件里写上你来自哪里。

sents.en: And that’s Ask a Teacher.
sents.zh: 以上就是本期《问问老师》。

sents.en: I’m Andrew Smith.
sents.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。

items.title: Apply and Application
items.titleZh: apply 和 application 的用法
items.series: Ask a Teacher 问问老师
items.summaryZh: 求职用 apply for，申请学校用 apply to，填表用 fill out；application 还指手机应用。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Andrew Smith wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English.

sents.en: This week on Ask a Teacher, we answer a question from Krystyna in Poland.
sents.zh: 本周的《问问老师》，我们来回答波兰的克里斯蒂娜提的问题。

sents.en: Here is Krystyna’s question:
sents.zh: 这是克里斯蒂娜的问题：

sents.en: Dear Teacher,
sents.zh: 亲爱的老师：

sents.en: I would like to know of different ways to use words such as “apply” and “application” for getting jobs or other purposes.
sents.zh: 我想知道 apply 和 application 这类词，在求职或其他场合有哪些不同的用法。

sents.en: Thank you, Krystyna.
sents.zh: 谢谢您。克里斯蒂娜

sents.en: I’m happy to answer this question, Krystyna.
sents.zh: 我很乐意回答这个问题，克里斯蒂娜。

sents.en: The word “apply” is a verb, and the word “application” is a noun.
sents.zh: apply 是动词，application 是名词。

sents.en: We can use both words when discussing the process of looking for a job.
sents.zh: 谈到找工作的过程时，这两个词都可以用。

sents.en: We say we “apply for a job” when we go through the official process of asking an employer for work.
sents.zh: 当我们通过正式流程向雇主申请工作时，我们说 apply for a job（申请工作）。

sents.en: To do this, we usually have to complete a job application.
sents.zh: 要申请，通常得填一份求职申请表（job application）。

sents.en: The application is a form, either online or on paper, that gives the employer information about the person applying for the job.
sents.zh: 申请表就是一份表格，可以是网上的，也可以是纸质的，用来向雇主提供申请人的信息。

sents.en: We commonly use the phrasal verb “fill out” to express the act of completing an application.
sents.zh: 我们常用短语动词 fill out 来表示填写申请表。

sents.en: Consider the following examples:
sents.zh: 看看下面的例子：

sents.en: You must fill out this application first.
sents.zh: 你得先填这份申请表。

sents.en: Did you fill out the application?
sents.zh: 申请表你填了吗？

sents.en: While we say “apply for” when trying to get a job, we say “apply to” when we are trying to get accepted into a school or other program, as in the following example:
sents.zh: 找工作时我们说 apply for，而想进入某所学校或某个项目时，我们说 apply to，比如下面这个例子：

sents.en: She applied to three medical schools in California.
sents.zh: 她申请了加州的三所医学院。

sents.en: However, we say “apply for” when we are trying to get financial aid or special awards.
sents.zh: 不过，申请助学金或特别奖项时，我们说 apply for。

sents.en: The expression “apply to” also has another meaning.
sents.zh: apply to 还有另一个意思。

sents.en: It can mean that something relates to something else, or that something is true for all people or things.
sents.zh: 它可以表示某事和另一件事有关，或者某件事对所有人、所有事物都适用。

sents.en: Listen to the following examples:
sents.zh: 听听下面的例子：

sents.en: The new rule only applies to people who work more than 40 hours each week.
sents.zh: 这条新规定只适用于每周工作超过 40 小时的人。

sents.en: The right of freedom of speech should apply to all citizens.
sents.zh: 言论自由的权利应当适用于所有公民。

sents.en: The word “application” has other meanings besides a form people fill out.
sents.zh: application 除了指人们填写的表格，还有别的意思。

sents.en: Among these is a computer program that does a specific task, or kind of work.
sents.zh: 其中之一是完成某项特定任务或工作的计算机程序。

sents.en: From this meaning, we get the term “Apps,” which we use in our smartphones and computers.
sents.zh: 由这个意思就有了 Apps（应用）这个词，也就是我们手机和电脑里用的那些应用。

sents.en: There also is another expression with the verb “apply.”
sents.zh: 动词 apply 还有一个表达。

sents.en: If you “apply yourself,” that means that you are working hard over a period of time to complete a project or develop a skill.
sents.zh: 如果你 apply yourself，意思是你在一段时间里努力投入，去完成一个项目或培养一项技能。

sents.en: For our readers and listeners, what are your questions about American English?
sents.zh: 各位读者和听众，你们有什么关于美国英语的问题吗？

sents.en: Are you applying yourself to your study of English?
sents.zh: 你在学英语这件事上用功了吗？

sents.en: We want to hear from you!
sents.zh: 我们很想听到你们的声音！

sents.en: Send us an email at learningenglish@voanews.com.
sents.zh: 请发邮件到 learningenglish@voanews.com。

sents.en: And please let us know where you are from, too.
sents.zh: 也请告诉我们你来自哪里。

sents.en: And that’s Ask a Teacher.
sents.zh: 以上就是本期《问问老师》。

sents.en: I’m Andrew Smith.
sents.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。

items.title: Spoiled Food and Drink
items.series: Ask a Teacher 问问老师
items.summaryZh: rotten、spoiled、gone bad、rancid、stale、wilted、moldy、sour——不同食物变质用不同的词。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Andrew Smith wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English.

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 大家好！

sents.en: This week on Ask a Teacher, we answer a question from Noura about how to describe food that is no longer safe to eat.
sents.zh: 本周的《问问老师》，我们来回答努拉的问题：怎样描述已经不能吃的食物。

sents.en: Dear Teacher,
sents.zh: 亲爱的老师：

sents.en: Would you please tell us the words we use to describe spoiled food?
sents.zh: 您能告诉我们，描述变质食物要用哪些词吗？

sents.en: Now I use only one or two words for all of food types, such as "rotten" or "spoiled."
sents.zh: 现在不管什么食物，我都只用一两个词，比如 rotten（腐烂的）或 spoiled（变质的）。

sents.en: However, in my native language we use different words for different categories like spoiled vegetables, bread, beverages, [and] meat-dishes.
sents.zh: 可是在我的母语里，不同种类的食物要用不同的词，比如坏掉的蔬菜、面包、饮料和肉菜。

sents.en: I wonder if it is the same in English too.
sents.zh: 我想知道英语是不是也这样。

sents.en: Thank you for writing to us, Noura.
sents.zh: 谢谢你的来信，努拉。

sents.en: I’m happy to answer this question.
sents.zh: 我很乐意回答这个问题。

sents.en: Let’s begin with the two words you mention, “rotten,” and “spoiled”.
sents.zh: 我们先从你提到的两个词说起：rotten 和 spoiled。

sents.en: We can use both words to talk about food in general.
sents.zh: 这两个词都可以泛指食物。

sents.en: So, we can say either of the following:
sents.zh: 所以下面两种说法都可以：

sents.en: That food is rotten.
sents.zh: 那食物烂了。

sents.en: That food is spoiled.
sents.zh: 那食物变质了。

sents.en: But for some foods, we use “rotten” much more than we use “spoiled.”
sents.zh: 不过对于某些食物，我们用 rotten 比用 spoiled 多得多。

sents.en: For example, we can say rotten eggs, rotten tomatoes, rotten apples, rotten vegetables, rotten fruit, and so on.
sents.zh: 比如我们说 rotten eggs（臭鸡蛋）、rotten tomatoes（烂番茄）、rotten apples（烂苹果）、烂蔬菜、烂水果等等。

sents.en: The most common usage of “rotten” is with eggs.
sents.zh: rotten 最常见的搭配是鸡蛋。

sents.en: We use “spoiled” mostly when talking about meat or milk.
sents.zh: spoiled 主要用来说肉或牛奶。

sents.en: Another general term for spoiled food or drink is the expression “gone bad”.
sents.zh: 形容食物或饮料变质，还有一个通用说法是 gone bad（坏了）。

sents.en: Now let’s look at some other terms we use with certain foods and drinks.
sents.zh: 下面我们来看看某些食物和饮料专用的一些说法。

sents.en: “Rancid” describes foods that contain fats that have started to go bad.
sents.zh: rancid 形容含油脂的食物开始变质，也就是“哈喇味”。

sents.en: These typically include nuts, seeds, and oils.
sents.zh: 这类食物通常包括坚果、种子和食用油。

sents.en: Fish, meat, and poultry can also become rancid.
sents.zh: 鱼、肉和禽肉也会变得 rancid。

sents.en: We use the word “stale” to describe bread that has become hard and difficult to eat.
sents.zh: 面包变硬、难以下咽，我们用 stale（不新鲜的、发硬的）。

sents.en: And “wilted” describes lettuce or other greens that are no longer fresh.
sents.zh: 而 wilted 形容生菜或其他绿叶菜蔫了、不新鲜了。

sents.en: Mold is a kind of very small fungus.
sents.zh: 霉菌是一种非常小的真菌。

sents.en: It makes food go bad and can be found on fruit, bread and cheese.
sents.zh: 它会让食物变质，水果、面包和奶酪上都可能长霉。

sents.en: The adjective we use for mold is “moldy.”
sents.zh: 形容发霉，我们用形容词 moldy。

sents.en: We use the adjective “sour” or the expression “to go sour” to describe milk or cream that has started to spoil.
sents.zh: 牛奶或奶油开始变质，我们用形容词 sour（酸的），或者说 to go sour（变酸）。

sents.en: Note that there is also a food called sour cream, which is safe to eat – and quite tasty!
sents.zh: 注意，还有一种食物叫 sour cream（酸奶油），它是可以放心吃的——而且很好吃！

sents.en: As you can see, a meal with rancid, stale, sour, wilted, moldy, rotten and spoiled food is one to avoid!
sents.zh: 所以你看，一顿饭里如果有哈喇的、发硬的、变酸的、蔫掉的、发霉的、腐烂的和变质的食物，最好别吃！

sents.en: For our readers and listeners, do you have a question about American English?
sents.zh: 各位读者和听众，你有关于美国英语的问题吗？

sents.en: Send us an email at learningenglish@voanews.com.
sents.zh: 请发邮件到 learningenglish@voanews.com。

sents.en: And that’s Ask a Teacher.
sents.zh: 以上就是本期《问问老师》。

sents.en: I’m Andrew Smith.
sents.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。

items.title: Near and Nearby
items.titleZh: near 和 nearby 的区别
items.series: Ask a Teacher 问问老师
items.summaryZh: nearby 可以放句尾、可以作形容词；near 要说出两个地点，还能作副词、构成复合形容词、作动词。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Andrew Smith wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English.

sents.en: Hello!
sents.zh: 大家好！

sents.en: This week on Ask a Teacher, we answer a question from Haruna in Japan about the usage of the words “near” and “nearby.”
sents.zh: 本周的《问问老师》，我们来回答日本的春菜提的问题：near 和 nearby 这两个词怎么用。

sents.en: Dear Teacher,
sents.zh: 亲爱的老师：

sents.en: Today, I have a question about two words, "near" and "nearby.”
sents.zh: 今天我有一个关于 near 和 nearby 这两个词的问题。

sents.en: What is [the] difference between these two words?
sents.zh: 这两个词有什么区别？

sents.en: Thank you and best regards,
sents.zh: 谢谢，致以问候，

sents.en: Haruna
sents.zh: 春菜

sents.en: I’m happy to answer this question, Haruna.
sents.zh: 我很乐意回答这个问题，春菜。

sents.en: Both words can mean “close in distance to something.”
sents.zh: 这两个词都可以表示“离某处距离近”。

sents.en: The word “near” also has other meanings, as we will see.
sents.zh: 不过我们后面会看到，near 还有别的意思。

sents.en: We can put the word “nearby” at the end of a sentence.
sents.zh: nearby 可以放在句子末尾。

sents.en: For example, if you are in someone’s house and a person in the house says:
sents.zh: 比如，你在别人家里，屋里有人说：

sents.en: The market is nearby.
sents.zh: 市场就在附近。

sents.en: That means the market is close to the house.
sents.zh: 意思是市场离这座房子很近。

sents.en: The speaker does not need to say the word “house” because the word “nearby” means close to the place already stated or known.
sents.zh: 说话的人不需要说出 house 这个词，因为 nearby 的意思就是离已经说过或大家都知道的地方很近。

sents.en: However, when we use the word “near” to say where something is, we say both places.
sents.zh: 不过，用 near 说明某物在哪里时，两个地方都要说出来。

sents.en: The following example shows this:
sents.zh: 下面这个例子就是这样：

sents.en: Their house is near the market.
sents.zh: 他们家在市场附近。

sents.en: The following two examples also show this difference in usage between “nearby” and “near”:
sents.zh: 下面两个例子也能看出 nearby 和 near 用法上的这个区别：

sents.en: The doctor’s office is nearby.
sents.zh: 诊所就在附近。

sents.en: The doctor’s office is near the bank.
sents.zh: 诊所在银行附近。

sents.en: We can also use “nearby” as an adjective before a noun, as in this example:
sents.zh: nearby 还可以作形容词放在名词前面，比如这个例子：

sents.en: Pollution from a nearby factory makes the air unhealthy to breathe.
sents.zh: 附近一家工厂的污染让空气变得不利于健康。

sents.en: Other uses of “near”
sents.zh: near 的其他用法

sents.en: Next, let’s look at three other ways we can use the word “near.”
sents.zh: 接下来，我们看看 near 的另外三种用法。

sents.en: We can use it as an adverb to express the idea that something will happen soon in the future, as in this example:
sents.zh: 它可以作副词，表示某事很快就要发生，比如这个例子：

sents.en: The end of our trip is near.
sents.zh: 我们的旅行快要结束了。

sents.en: We can also use “near” as a compound adjective, as in the following example:
sents.zh: near 还可以用来构成复合形容词，比如下面这个例子：

sents.en: That old car is still in near-perfect condition.
sents.zh: 那辆旧车的车况仍然近乎完美。

sents.en: Remember that when we write compound adjectives, we must put a hyphen, or short line, connecting the two adjectives.
sents.zh: 记住，写复合形容词时，两个词之间要加连字符，也就是一条短横线。

sents.en: Lastly, we can use the word “near” as a verb, meaning “getting close to in time,” as in this example:
sents.zh: 最后，near 还可以作动词，意思是“在时间上接近”，比如这个例子：

sents.en: The building project is nearing completion.
sents.zh: 这个建筑项目快要完工了。

sents.en: For our readers and listeners, what are your questions about American English?
sents.zh: 各位读者和听众，你们有什么关于美国英语的问题吗？

sents.en: We’d like to hear from you.
sents.zh: 我们很想听到你们的声音。

sents.en: Send us an email at learningenglish@voanews.com.
sents.zh: 请发邮件到 learningenglish@voanews.com。

sents.en: And please include where you are from in your email, too.
sents.zh: 也请在邮件里写上你来自哪里。

sents.en: And that’s Ask a Teacher.
sents.zh: 以上就是本期《问问老师》。

sents.en: I’m Andrew Smith.
sents.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。

items.title: Minimal Pairs for Pronunciation
items.series: Ask a Teacher 问问老师
items.summaryZh: 为什么 crash 和 clash 听着一样？母语里没有的音很难听出来。用 hit/heat、rake/lake 这样的最小对立词训练耳朵和舌头。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Andrew Smith wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English.

sents.en: This week on Ask a Teacher we answer a question from Doraemon in Japan.
sents.zh: 本周的《问问老师》，我们来回答日本的哆啦A梦提的问题。

sents.en: Here is Doraemon’s question:
sents.zh: 这是哆啦A梦的问题：

sents.en: Hi VOA,
sents.zh: 你好，VOA：

sents.en: For me, as an English learner, words like clash, crash, and crush sound like the same word.
sents.zh: 作为英语学习者，clash、crash 和 crush 这几个词在我听来像是同一个词。

sents.en: Can you help me to tell one word from others?
sents.zh: 你们能帮我把它们区分开吗？

sents.en: Thank you.
sents.zh: 谢谢。

sents.en: I’m happy to answer this question, Doraemon.
sents.zh: 我很乐意回答这个问题，哆啦A梦。

sents.en: When a foreign language contains sounds that do not exist in a person’s native language, it can be difficult for learners to hear those sounds.
sents.zh: 当一门外语里有学习者母语中不存在的音时，学习者可能很难听出这些音。

sents.en: The reason you have difficulty hearing the difference between “crash” and “clash” is because the Japanese language does not have the consonant sounds “r” or “l.”
sents.zh: 你很难听出 crash 和 clash 的区别，是因为日语里没有 r 和 l 这两个辅音。

sents.en: And when English speakers are talking quickly, the difference between the sounds of “r” and “l” becomes very small.
sents.zh: 而且英语母语者说得快的时候，r 和 l 的差别会变得非常小。

sents.en: As a result, those two consonants can sound the same to a native Japanese speaker.
sents.zh: 结果，对日语母语者来说，这两个辅音听起来可能一模一样。

sents.en: Some vowel sounds can also be difficult to hear or pronounce depending on the vowels a person’s native language has.
sents.zh: 有些元音也可能难听出来、难发出来，这取决于一个人的母语里有哪些元音。

sents.en: For example, consider the difference between the following two words:
sents.zh: 比如，想想下面这两个词的区别：

sents.en: hit heat
sents.zh: hit 和 heat

sents.en: The Spanish language has the vowel sound in the word “heat,” but it does not have the vowel sound in the word “hit.”
sents.zh: 西班牙语里有 heat 中的那个元音，却没有 hit 中的元音。

sents.en: As a result, Spanish speakers will sometimes pronounce words like “hit,” “bit,” and “little” with an “ee” sound.
sents.zh: 所以，说西班牙语的人有时会把 hit、bit、little 这类词里的元音发成 ee 的音。

sents.en: For example, the two words “hit” and “heat” will both sound like “heat” when spoken with a Spanish accent.
sents.zh: 比如，hit 和 heat 这两个词，用西班牙口音说出来听着都像 heat。

sents.en: You can learn to hear the difference between sounds in a foreign language by careful practice using minimal pairs.
sents.zh: 通过认真练习最小对立词，你可以学会听出外语里不同发音的区别。

sents.en: Minimal pairs are two words that differ from each other by only one sound.
sents.zh: 最小对立词是只差一个音的两个词。

sents.en: For example, the two words “hit” and “heat” differ from each other by only one sound.
sents.zh: 比如，hit 和 heat 这两个词就只差一个音。

sents.en: Here are some tips for using minimal pairs:
sents.zh: 下面是使用最小对立词的一些建议：

sents.en: Find lists and recordings of minimal pairs through a Google search or on YouTube.
sents.zh: 可以通过谷歌搜索或在 YouTube 上找最小对立词的词表和录音。

sents.en: For Japanese speakers, find minimal pairs that differ between the sounds of “r” and “l.”
sents.zh: 说日语的人可以找 r 和 l 对立的最小对立词。

sents.en: Be sure to include minimal pairs that place the two sounds at the beginning, middle, and end of words.
sents.zh: 一定要包括这两个音分别出现在词首、词中和词尾的例子。

sents.en: Here are examples:
sents.zh: 下面是一些例子：

sents.en: rake lake
sents.zh: rake 和 lake

sents.en: correct collect
sents.zh: correct 和 collect

sents.en: hair hail
sents.zh: hair 和 hail

sents.en: Carefully listen to the pronunciation of the minimal pairs.
sents.zh: 仔细听这些最小对立词的发音。

sents.en: At first, it might be difficult for you to hear the difference between them.
sents.zh: 一开始，你可能很难听出它们的区别。

sents.en: But over time you will start hearing the difference.
sents.zh: 但时间长了，你就会开始听出区别。

sents.en: Also practice pronouncing these sounds.
sents.zh: 也要练习发这些音。

sents.en: Learning to pronounce them can help you hear them.
sents.zh: 学会发这些音，能帮助你听出它们。

sents.en: To pronounce them, you need to practice putting your tongue in the correct position.
sents.zh: 要发好这些音，你需要练习把舌头放到正确的位置。

sents.en: The tongue is a muscle.
sents.zh: 舌头是一块肌肉。

sents.en: Just as we can train our muscles to play a sport, we can train our tongue to move to the correct positions for pronouncing a foreign language.
sents.zh: 就像我们可以训练肌肉去做运动一样，我们也可以训练舌头移动到说外语所需的正确位置。

sents.en: This How to Pronounce video from VOA Learning English shows the tongue positions you need to pronounce the letters “r” and “l” correctly.
sents.zh: VOA 慢速英语的这期《怎么读》视频，演示了正确发 r 和 l 时舌头该放在哪里。

sents.en: For our readers and listeners, what are your questions about American English?
sents.zh: 各位读者和听众，你们有什么关于美国英语的问题吗？

sents.en: We want to hear from you!
sents.zh: 我们很想听到你们的声音！

sents.en: Send us an email at learningenglish@voanews.com.
sents.zh: 请发邮件到 learningenglish@voanews.com。

sents.en: And please let us know where you are from, too.
sents.zh: 也请告诉我们你来自哪里。

sents.en: And that’s Ask a Teacher.
sents.zh: 以上就是本期《问问老师》。

sents.en: I’m Andrew Smith.
sents.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。

items.title: Simple Past and Present Perfect
items.titleZh: 一般过去时 vs 现在完成时
items.series: Everyday Grammar 日常语法
items.summaryZh: I saw the movie 和 I have seen the movie 有什么不同？具体时间用过去时；重复、for/since、never、ever 用现在完成时。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Adam Brock wrote and produced this story for VOA Learning English. Jill Robbins was the editor.

sents.en: In this week’s episode of Everyday Grammar, we’re going to help you understand the difference between the simple past and the present perfect.
sents.zh: 在本期《日常语法》里，我们来帮你弄懂一般过去时和现在完成时的区别。

sents.en: English learners often confuse these two verb tenses.
sents.zh: 英语学习者经常把这两种时态搞混。

sents.en: Let’s start with an example.
sents.zh: 我们先看一个例子。

sents.en: Can you tell the difference between these two sentences?
sents.zh: 你能说出下面这两个句子的区别吗？

sents.en: Sentence one: I saw the movie.
sents.zh: 第一句：I saw the movie.（我看了那部电影。）

sents.en: Sentence two: I have seen the movie.
sents.zh: 第二句：I have seen the movie.（我看过那部电影。）

sents.en: Sentence one uses the simple past tense.
sents.zh: 第一句用的是一般过去时。

sents.en: Sentence two uses the present perfect tense.
sents.zh: 第二句用的是现在完成时。

sents.en: “I saw the movie” and “I have seen the movie” both refer to an action that was finished in the past.
sents.zh: “I saw the movie” 和 “I have seen the movie” 说的都是过去已经完成的动作。

sents.en: But there is one important difference: “I saw the movie” suggests that you saw the movie at a specific time in the past.
sents.zh: 但有一个重要区别：“I saw the movie” 暗示你是在过去某个具体时间看的。

sents.en: “I have seen the movie” suggests that you saw the movie at an unknown time in the past.
sents.zh: “I have seen the movie” 则暗示你是在过去某个不确定的时间看的。

sents.en: Use the simple past to talk about a finished action that happened at a specific time.
sents.zh: 说在某个具体时间发生、已经结束的动作，用一般过去时。

sents.en: For example, “I went out with my friends last night.”
sents.zh: 比如，“I went out with my friends last night.”（我昨晚和朋友出去了。）

sents.en: The adverb “last night” is not required, but it does help clarify that the event happened at a specific time.
sents.zh: 副词 last night 不是必须的，但它确实能说明这件事发生在一个具体时间。

sents.en: That’s the easy part.
sents.zh: 这部分比较简单。

sents.en: Now let’s talk about the present perfect.
sents.zh: 下面我们来说说现在完成时。

sents.en: You form the present perfect by using “have” or “has” followed by the past participle form of the verb.
sents.zh: 现在完成时的构成是 have 或 has 加上动词的过去分词。

sents.en: For example, “I have graduated from college.”
sents.zh: 比如，“I have graduated from college.”（我已经大学毕业了。）

sents.en: The present perfect confuses English learners because it refers to a past action.
sents.zh: 现在完成时让英语学习者困惑，是因为它说的是过去的动作。

sents.en: It is also called “present perfect” because speakers use it to stress the importance of a past event in the present.
sents.zh: 它之所以叫“现在”完成时，是因为说话人用它来强调过去的事对现在的意义。

sents.en: The sentence “I have graduated from college,” emphasizes the present effect of a past event -- graduation.
sents.zh: “I have graduated from college” 这句话强调的是过去的事——毕业——对现在的影响。

sents.en: The exact time of the graduation is not important.
sents.zh: 具体什么时候毕业的并不重要。

sents.en: There are four more common situations that require the present perfect.
sents.zh: 还有四种常见情况需要用现在完成时。

sents.en: First, it can express a repeated action.
sents.zh: 第一，它可以表示重复发生的动作。

sents.en: When an action happened more than one time in the past, use the present perfect.
sents.zh: 一个动作在过去发生过不止一次，就用现在完成时。

sents.en: For example,
sents.zh: 比如，

sents.en: “I have seen the movie three times."
sents.zh: “I have seen the movie three times.”（这部电影我看过三遍。）

sents.en: Second, it is common to use the present perfect with the words “for” and “since.”
sents.zh: 第二，现在完成时常和 for 和 since 一起用。

sents.en: “For” and “since” are adverbs that tell about the duration of an activity.
sents.zh: for 和 since 是说明某个活动持续多久的副词。

sents.en: They answer the question “how long?”
sents.zh: 它们回答“多长时间？”这个问题。

sents.en: For example,
sents.zh: 比如，

sents.en: “I have studied English for a long time."
sents.zh: “I have studied English for a long time.”（我学英语已经很久了。）

sents.en: Third, the negative adverb “never” requires the present perfect.
sents.zh: 第三，否定副词 never 要求用现在完成时。

sents.en: You can say,
sents.zh: 你可以说，

sents.en: “I have never been to France.”
sents.zh: “I have never been to France.”（我从没去过法国。）

sents.en: You would not say,
sents.zh: 不会说，

sents.en: “I did never go to France.”
sents.zh: “I did never go to France.”

sents.en: Finally, when asking a question in the present perfect, use “ever,” as in,
sents.zh: 最后，用现在完成时提问时，要用 ever，比如，

sents.en: “Have you ever won the lottery?”
sents.zh: “Have you ever won the lottery?”（你中过彩票吗？）

sents.en: Here’s a tip: pay close attention to adverbs.
sents.zh: 给你一个小窍门：多留意副词。

sents.en: Adverbs give hints, or clues, about which verb tense you should use.
sents.zh: 副词会给出提示或线索，告诉你该用哪种时态。

sents.en: A good way to practice the present perfect is to ask an English-speaking friend if he or she has ever done something.
sents.zh: 练习现在完成时的一个好办法，是问说英语的朋友有没有做过某件事。

sents.en: “Have you ever flown in an airplane?”
sents.zh: “Have you ever flown in an airplane?”（你坐过飞机吗？）

sents.en: or
sents.zh: 或者

sents.en: “Have you ever seen the Grand Canyon?”
sents.zh: “Have you ever seen the Grand Canyon?”（你见过大峡谷吗？）

sents.en: I’m Ashley Thompson.
sents.zh: 我是阿什莉·汤普森。

sents.en: And I’m Jonathan Evans.
sents.zh: 我是乔纳森·埃文斯。

items.title: It’s 'Kind of Just' Hedging
items.series: Everyday Grammar 日常语法
items.summaryZh: It kind of just saps your motivation 怎么理解？kind of 和 just 都是修饰语，用来缓和语气、照顾对方感受。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Jill Robbins wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English.

sents.en: This week on Everyday Grammar, we answer a question from Kyosuke, a loyal reader in Japan, who asks:
sents.zh: 本周的《日常语法》，我们来回答日本的忠实读者恭介的问题，他问：

sents.en: I have a question about the article "When Colleges Close, Some Students Never Go Back."
sents.zh: 我对《大学关门后，一些学生再也没回去上学》这篇文章有个疑问。
