sents.en: It reads, “It kind of just saps your motivation to do anything.”
sents.zh: 文章里有一句：“It kind of just saps your motivation to do anything.”

sents.en: I was not able to understand the structure and meaning of this sentence.
sents.zh: 我没看懂这句话的结构和意思。

sents.en: What is the subject and what is the verb?
sents.zh: 主语是什么？谓语动词是什么？

sents.en: Especially, I didn't realize (the meaning of) "it kind of just.”
sents.zh: 尤其是 it kind of just（是什么意思），我没弄明白。

sents.en: The story Kyosuke read told about how the University of the Arts in Philadelphia closed suddenly.
sents.zh: 恭介读的那篇报道讲的是费城艺术大学突然关闭的事。

sents.en: That affected a lot of students.
sents.zh: 这件事影响了很多学生。

sents.en: One first-year student there was unsure of his next steps.
sents.zh: 那里的一名大一学生不确定下一步该怎么办。

sents.en: He said he did not know where to start looking for another place to study.
sents.zh: 他说他不知道该从哪儿开始找别的学校读书。

sents.en: Let us look at the structure of the statement first.
sents.zh: 我们先看看这句话的结构。

sents.en: It kind of just saps your motivation to do anything.
sents.zh: It kind of just saps your motivation to do anything.（这件事多少有点让人做什么都提不起劲。）

sents.en: The subject is “It” -- a pronoun that refers to the school closing.
sents.zh: 主语是 It，一个代词，指的是学校关闭这件事。

sents.en: The verb is “sap” which means to use up the supply of something.
sents.zh: 动词是 sap，意思是把某样东西的储备耗光。

sents.en: We often use it to talk about reducing energy or strength.
sents.zh: 我们常用它来说消耗精力或体力。

sents.en: Here is an example:
sents.zh: 举个例子：

sents.en: Waiting in the long line at the store sapped my energy.
sents.zh: 在商店排长队把我的精力都耗光了。

sents.en: In the student’s statement, the verb “sap” has a direct object – motivation.
sents.zh: 在这个学生的话里，动词 sap 带了一个直接宾语——motivation（动力）。

sents.en: He is saying that he has less desire now to apply to other schools.
sents.zh: 他是说，他现在不太想去申请别的学校了。

sents.en: The next part of the statement is “kind of.”
sents.zh: 这句话的下一部分是 kind of。

sents.en: This phrase is in the group of words we call “qualifiers.”
sents.zh: 这个短语属于我们称为“修饰语”的一类词。

sents.en: A qualifier is a word, usually an adjective or adverb, that changes the meaning of another word or phrase.
sents.zh: 修饰语通常是形容词或副词，用来改变另一个词或短语的意思。

sents.en: Some qualifiers strengthen the force of a statement, like “very” and “too.”
sents.zh: 有些修饰语会加强语气，比如 very 和 too。

sents.en: Others weaken the force, like “somewhat” and “seem.”
sents.zh: 有些则会减弱语气，比如 somewhat 和 seem。

sents.en: In his statement, the student uses “kind of just” before the verb “sap” to show he is not firmly saying that the event has had this effect.
sents.zh: 这个学生在动词 sap 前面用了 kind of just，表示他并不是很肯定地说这件事带来了这样的影响。

sents.en: We can say he is hedging.
sents.zh: 我们可以说他在“打预防针”，也就是留有余地。

sents.en: A “hedge” in language is often a way to express uncertainty or reduce the force of a statement.
sents.zh: 语言里的 hedge（留余地）常常是用来表达不确定，或减弱一句话的语气。

sents.en: For example, if you do not want to stay at a party you might tell a friend:
sents.zh: 比如，你不想在聚会上待下去，可能会跟朋友说：

sents.en: I’m kind of tired, can we leave the party a little early?
sents.zh: 我有点累了，我们能早点离开聚会吗？

sents.en: You are not saying you are very tired and need to leave immediately; you simply want to introduce the idea of leaving early.
sents.zh: 你并不是说你累坏了、必须马上走，只是想提出早点走的想法。

sents.en: Using “kind of” is one way that speakers preserve their relationships with others.
sents.zh: 用 kind of 是说话人维护和别人关系的一种方式。

sents.en: For example, a friend asks you if you like the band playing at an event.
sents.zh: 比如，在一个活动上，朋友问你喜不喜欢正在演出的乐队。

sents.en: You might answer:
sents.zh: 你可能会回答：

sents.en: Their music is okay, but it’s kind of loud for me.
sents.zh: 他们的音乐还行，就是对我来说有点吵。

sents.en: You might think the music is much too loud, or even bad, but if your friend likes it, you do not want to hurt their feelings.
sents.zh: 你可能觉得音乐太吵，甚至很难听，但如果朋友喜欢，你不想伤他的心。

sents.en: So, you can hedge, or protect their feelings, by using “kind of.”
sents.zh: 所以你可以用 kind of 来缓和一下，照顾对方的感受。

sents.en: Another part of the statement our reader asked about is the word “just.”
sents.zh: 读者问到的另一部分是 just 这个词。

sents.en: It is also a qualifier.
sents.zh: 它也是一个修饰语。

sents.en: “Just” can change the meaning of the words that follow.
sents.zh: just 可以改变它后面那些词的意思。

sents.en: In such a case, it can mean “nothing more than” or “only.”
sents.zh: 这种情况下，它的意思是“只不过”或“仅仅”。

sents.en: For example, if you are at an event with a friend, they might ask:
sents.zh: 比如，你和朋友在看演出，朋友可能会问：

sents.en: Why do you keep checking the time?
sents.zh: 你为什么老看时间？

sents.en: Aren’t you enjoying the show?
sents.zh: 你不喜欢这个演出吗？

sents.en: You might answer,
sents.zh: 你可能会回答：

sents.en: I just don’t want to miss the last bus.
sents.zh: 我只是不想错过末班车。

sents.en: It’s getting late.
sents.zh: 时间不早了。

sents.en: I hope this helps you understand the expression better, Kyosuke.
sents.zh: 恭介，希望这能帮你更好地理解这个表达。

sents.en: Do you have a question about English Grammar?
sents.zh: 你有关于英语语法的问题吗？

sents.en: Write to us at learningenglish@voanews.com.
sents.zh: 请写信到 learningenglish@voanews.com。

sents.en: And that’s Everyday Grammar!
sents.zh: 以上就是本期《日常语法》！

sents.en: I’m Jill Robbins.
sents.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

items.title: Learn 10 Separable Phrasal Verbs
items.series: Everyday Grammar 日常语法
items.summaryZh: 短语动词是“动词 + 小品词”，整体一个意思。throw out my jeans 和 throw my jeans out 都对，但代词必须放中间：throw them out。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Jill Robbins and Adam Brock wrote this lesson for Learning English. George Grow was the editor.

sents.en: Welcome back to Everyday Grammar from VOA Learning English.
sents.zh: 欢迎回到 VOA 慢速英语的《日常语法》。

sents.en: Today we return to a very common verb form in English – phrasal verbs.
sents.zh: 今天我们再来讲英语里一种非常常见的动词形式——短语动词。

sents.en: You will find one phrasal verb in every 192 words of written English.
sents.zh: 在书面英语里，平均每 192 个词就会出现一个短语动词。

sents.en: They will make your English sound more natural once you begin using them correctly.
sents.zh: 一旦你开始正确使用它们，你的英语听起来会更自然。

sents.en: In an earlier program, we explained how and why English speakers use them.
sents.zh: 在之前的节目里，我们讲过说英语的人如何、以及为什么使用短语动词。

sents.en: Today we look at some often-used phrasal verbs.
sents.zh: 今天我们来看一些常用的短语动词。

sents.en: This type of phrasal verb allows a direct object to come between the verb and the preposition or adverb.
sents.zh: 这类短语动词允许直接宾语插在动词和介词或副词之间。

sents.en: As you will hear, there is a special rule that learners should know about when using these 10 phrasal verbs.
sents.zh: 你会听到，使用这 10 个短语动词时，有一条学习者应该知道的特别规则。

sents.en: The structure of phrasal verbs
sents.zh: 短语动词的结构

sents.en: As you know, a phrasal verb is a phrase with two or more words: a verb and a preposition or adverb or both.
sents.zh: 你知道，短语动词是由两个或更多词组成的短语：一个动词，加上一个介词或副词，或者两者都有。

sents.en: We call the preposition or adverb a particle when it combines with a verb.
sents.zh: 介词或副词和动词结合时，我们叫它“小品词”。

sents.en: Here are two examples:
sents.zh: 这里有两个例子：

sents.en: Please put the lamp on the desk.
sents.zh: 请把台灯放在桌子上。

sents.en: I think you're putting me on.
sents.zh: 我觉得你在逗我。

sents.en: In the first sentence, on is a preposition showing the position of the lamp.
sents.zh: 第一句里，on 是介词，表示台灯的位置。

sents.en: In the second sentence, on is an adverbial particle.
sents.zh: 第二句里，on 是副词小品词。

sents.en: Put on is a phrasal verb meaning "fool" or "trick" in this sentence.
sents.zh: 在这句话里，put on 是短语动词，意思是“愚弄”或“捉弄”。

sents.en: An important point is that a regular verb+preposition combination has two meanings.
sents.zh: 要点在于，普通的“动词 + 介词”组合有两个各自的意思。

sents.en: A phrasal verb, that is, a verb+particle, has a single meaning within a sentence.
sents.zh: 而短语动词，也就是“动词 + 小品词”，在句子里只有一个整体意思。

sents.en: Many phrasal verbs have a number of different meanings in different situations.
sents.zh: 很多短语动词在不同场合有好几个不同的意思。

sents.en: Yet the meaning of the verb+particle can usually be expressed with a single Latin-based verb.
sents.zh: 不过，“动词 + 小品词”的意思通常可以用一个源自拉丁语的动词来表达。

sents.en: Here are two sentences with the same meaning:
sents.zh: 下面两句话意思相同：

sents.en: They tore down the old building.
sents.zh: 他们拆掉了那栋旧楼。

sents.en: They demolished the old building.
sents.zh: 他们拆除了那栋旧楼。

sents.en: The verb tear has its own meaning, and so does the preposition down.
sents.zh: 动词 tear 有它自己的意思，介词 down 也有它自己的意思。

sents.en: They can combine with other words when they are alone.
sents.zh: 它们单独使用时可以和别的词搭配。

sents.en: But as a phrasal verb, tear down, they have one meaning: "destroy."
sents.zh: 但作为短语动词 tear down，它们只有一个意思：“摧毁、拆掉”。

sents.en: In 1987, U.S. President Ronald Reagan visited West Germany.
sents.zh: 1987 年，美国总统罗纳德·里根访问西德。

sents.en: He told a crowd in the divided city of Berlin, "Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!"
sents.zh: 他在分裂的柏林城对人群说：“戈尔巴乔夫先生，推倒这堵墙！”

sents.en: Now for the tricky part.
sents.zh: 下面是比较难的部分。

sents.en: You know that some verbs are transitive, which means they have a direct object.
sents.zh: 你知道有些动词是及物动词，也就是带直接宾语的动词。

sents.en: When such verbs appear as phrasal verbs, an object can either separate the phrase or follow it.
sents.zh: 这类动词构成短语动词时，宾语既可以插在短语中间，也可以跟在后面。

sents.en: Here’s an example.
sents.zh: 举个例子。

sents.en: I decided to throw out my old jeans.
sents.zh: 我决定扔掉我的旧牛仔裤。（throw out my old jeans）

sents.en: I decided to throw my old jeans out.
sents.zh: 我决定把我的旧牛仔裤扔掉。（throw my old jeans out）

sents.en: Both of these sentences are correct.
sents.zh: 这两句都对。

sents.en: The object of the phrasal verb throw out is jeans.
sents.zh: 短语动词 throw out 的宾语是 jeans（牛仔裤）。

sents.en: You can use a pronoun instead of jeans and ask,
sents.zh: 你可以用代词代替 jeans，问：

sents.en: Are you sure you want to throw them out?
sents.zh: 你确定要把它们扔掉吗？

sents.en: However, you cannot ask, "Are you sure you want to throw out them?"
sents.zh: 但是，你不能问 “Are you sure you want to throw out them?”

sents.en: Here, the pronoun them must appear between the verb and the particle.
sents.zh: 这里，代词 them 必须放在动词和小品词中间。

sents.en: In recent years, language experts began to use computers to examine a large collection, or corpus, of written and spoken language.
sents.zh: 近年来，语言专家开始用计算机分析大量书面语和口语材料，也就是语料库。

sents.en: When researchers look for phrasal verbs, they find that many deal with an activity.
sents.zh: 研究人员寻找短语动词时发现，很多短语动词都和某种活动有关。

sents.en: They also find a few verbs combine with many particles.
sents.zh: 他们还发现，少数几个动词能和很多小品词搭配。

sents.en: Among the most common verbs are come, put, get, go, pick, sit and take.
sents.zh: 最常见的动词有 come、put、get、go、pick、sit 和 take。

sents.en: These combine with the adverb particles up, out, in, on, off, and down to make up a group of very useful phrasal verbs.
sents.zh: 它们和副词小品词 up、out、in、on、off、down 搭配，构成了一组非常有用的短语动词。

sents.en: Now, let’s look at transitive phrasal verbs.
sents.zh: 下面我们来看及物短语动词。

sents.en: See the list at the end of the article.
sents.zh: 请看文章末尾的列表。

sents.en: The verb get is part of many phrasal verbs.
sents.zh: 动词 get 是很多短语动词的一部分。

sents.en: For example, we use get up to mean "to wake oneself up" or "to awaken someone."
sents.zh: 比如，get up 的意思是“自己起床”或“把某人叫醒”。

sents.en: For example:
sents.zh: 例如：

sents.en: My son loves to sleep late.
sents.zh: 我儿子特别爱睡懒觉。

sents.en: I got him up on time to catch the bus this morning.
sents.zh: 今天早上我按时把他叫起来去赶公交。

sents.en: Remember, the pronoun has to come between the verb and the adverb, so we cannot say, "I got up him."
sents.zh: 记住，代词必须放在动词和副词之间，所以不能说 “I got up him.”

items.title: Tips for Better Conversations in English at Work
items.titleZh: 工作中用英语和客户沟通
items.series: Education Tips 学习技巧
items.summaryZh: 四个听力策略：预判对方会说什么、专注听关键词、请对方说慢点或澄清、提前预演回答。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Jill Robbins wrote this story for VOA Learning English. Ashley Thompson was the editor.

sents.en: When we are learning a new language, carrying on a conversation can be difficult.
sents.zh: 学一门新语言的时候，和人聊下去可能很难。

sents.en: It is even harder when there is the added pressure of doing a job well using the new language.
sents.zh: 如果还要用这门新语言把工作做好，压力更大，就更难了。

sents.en: One of our readers, Emre, works at a job that requires him to talk with customers in English.
sents.zh: 我们的一位读者埃姆雷，他的工作需要用英语和客户交谈。

sents.en: He recently asked for advice on how he can improve his listening skills.
sents.zh: 他最近来信，想知道怎样提高听力。

sents.en: There are probably many other readers who use English in their daily work, too.
sents.zh: 可能还有很多读者在日常工作中也要用英语。

sents.en: So today, we will suggest some simple learning strategies to improve your ability to listen and carry on conversations.
sents.zh: 所以今天，我们来推荐一些简单的学习策略，帮你提高听力和把对话进行下去的能力。

sents.en: A learning strategy can be a thought or an action you take to make learning easier.
sents.zh: 学习策略可以是一个想法，也可以是一个行动，目的是让学习更轻松。

sents.en: Here are four strategies for you to consider.
sents.zh: 下面四个策略供你参考。

sents.en: Predict
sents.zh: 预判

sents.en: The first strategy is to predict what you will hear.
sents.zh: 第一个策略是预判你会听到什么。

sents.en: Maybe your customers sometimes say they have problems with placing an order on your website.
sents.zh: 也许你的客户有时会说，他们在你们网站上下单时遇到了问题。

sents.en: You can think about the ways they usually ask about that problem.
sents.zh: 你可以想想，他们问这个问题时通常会怎么说。

sents.en: What words do they often use in that kind of conversation?
sents.zh: 在这类对话里，他们常用哪些词？

sents.en: For example, customers may often use the word “order.”
sents.zh: 比如，客户可能经常用到 order（订单、下单）这个词。

sents.en: Focus
sents.zh: 专注

sents.en: The next strategy is to prepare a list of those words and listen for them when a customer begins talking with you.
sents.zh: 下一个策略是把这些词列成清单，客户一开口就专门听这些词。

sents.en: I call this “focusing when you listen.”
sents.zh: 我把这叫作“带着重点去听”。

sents.en: The next time you are listening to a customer, pay attention to the key words that help you understand their question.
sents.zh: 下次听客户说话时，留意那些能帮你听懂对方问题的关键词。

sents.en: Ask
sents.zh: 提问

sents.en: Next, think about what you can say to the customer to let them know you need a little help understanding them.
sents.zh: 接下来，想想可以对客户说些什么，让对方知道你需要一点帮助才能听懂。

sents.en: You can let the customer know you are an English learner.
sents.zh: 你可以告诉客户你正在学英语。

sents.en: There are two questions you can ask.
sents.zh: 有两种问题可以问。

sents.en: At the beginning of the conversation, you can ask, “Would you please speak more slowly?”
sents.zh: 对话一开始，你可以问：“Would you please speak more slowly?”（您能说慢一点吗？）

sents.en: The other kind of question is one I call, “asking to clarify.”
sents.zh: 另一种问题，我叫它“请对方澄清”。

sents.en: Remember, you predicted some of the words your customers may use.
sents.zh: 记住，你已经预判过客户可能会用的一些词。

sents.en: You should listen closely for those words.
sents.zh: 你要仔细听这些词。

sents.en: When you hear one, you can ask the customer a short question to be sure.
sents.zh: 听到其中一个时，就可以问客户一个简短的问题来确认。

sents.en: “Did you say you want to order?”
sents.zh: “Did you say you want to order?”（您是说想下单吗？）

sents.en: Rehearse
sents.zh: 预演

sents.en: You can prepare your answers to customers’ questions and rehearse them in your free time.
sents.zh: 你可以提前准备好对客户问题的回答，在空闲时间预演。

sents.en: You may want to keep a notebook with your usual answers.
sents.zh: 你可以准备一个本子，记下你常用的回答。

sents.en: You can practice saying them out loud to yourself.
sents.zh: 可以自己大声练习说出来。

sents.en: Finally, you can put all these actions and thoughts together.
sents.zh: 最后，你可以把这些做法和思路结合起来。

sents.en: Let’s say a customer calls and says:
sents.zh: 假设一位客户打电话来说：

sents.en: I want to order some face cream but I cannot find the button for ordering.
sents.zh: 我想订一些面霜，可是找不到下单的按钮。

sents.en: You are not sure of the product the customer wants.
sents.zh: 你不确定客户要的是哪个产品。

sents.en: But you did note the words “order” and “button,” so you can ask a question to clarify the customer’s request.
sents.zh: 但你注意到了 order 和 button 这两个词，所以可以问一个问题来弄清客户的需求。

sents.en: You rehearsed this question:
sents.zh: 你预演过这个问题：

sents.en: Are you looking for the button to order?
sents.zh: 您是在找下单按钮吗？

sents.en: The customer says, “Yes.”
sents.zh: 客户说：“是的。”

sents.en: Then, you can ask another question that you practiced.
sents.zh: 然后，你可以再问一个练过的问题。

sents.en: May I ask the name of the product you want to order?
sents.zh: 请问您想订的产品叫什么名字？

sents.en: We hope that these four strategies will help you to better deal with your customers in English.
sents.zh: 希望这四个策略能帮你更好地用英语应对客户。

sents.en: Learning English takes time and effort, but sometimes a few good strategies make things easier.
sents.zh: 学英语需要时间和努力，但有时几个好策略就能让事情容易一些。

sents.en: Another way you can prepare is to listen to English movies and podcasts as often as you can.
sents.zh: 另一个准备方法是尽可能多听英语电影和播客。

sents.en: The more you listen to conversations in English, the more you will understand over time.
sents.zh: 英语对话听得越多，时间长了你能听懂的就越多。

sents.en: I’m Jill Robbins.
sents.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

items.title: Make a Habit of Learning English
items.series: Education Tips 学习技巧
items.summaryZh: 习惯由提示、渴望、反应、奖励四步形成。让学英语变得显眼、有吸引力、简单、有满足感，从每天两分钟开始。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: John Russell wrote this story for Learning English. Bryan Lynn was the editor.

sents.en: Since the beginning of the coronavirus crisis, many people have had to change their habits, or usual ways of doing things.
sents.zh: 新冠疫情开始以来，很多人不得不改变自己的习惯，也就是平时做事的方式。

sents.en: Some people who used to go to school now study at home.
sents.zh: 一些原来去学校上学的人，现在在家学习。

sents.en: Some of them have been trying to get in the habit of learning and studying on their own.
sents.zh: 其中有些人一直在努力养成自主学习的习惯。

sents.en: How might habits connect with studying and learning?
sents.zh: 习惯和学习之间可能有什么关系？

sents.en: Today’s Education Tips will explore that very question.
sents.zh: 今天的《学习技巧》就来探讨这个问题。

sents.en: What are habits?
sents.zh: 什么是习惯？

sents.en: Habits are regular ways of dealing with your environment.
sents.zh: 习惯是你应对周围环境的固定方式。

sents.en: You generally do not pay attention to them.
sents.zh: 你通常不会注意到它们。

sents.en: In the book Good Habits, Bad Habits, Dr. Wendy Wood notes that “A habit turns the world around you—your context—into a trigger to act.”
sents.zh: 温迪·伍德博士在《好习惯，坏习惯》一书中指出：“习惯把你周围的世界——也就是你所处的情境——变成了行动的触发器。”

sents.en: Habits take many forms – eating, exercising, even studying.
sents.zh: 习惯有很多种——吃饭、锻炼，甚至学习。

sents.en: You may not realize it, but habits make up many of the actions that you do every day.
sents.zh: 你可能没意识到，但你每天做的很多事都是习惯。

sents.en: How are habits made?
sents.zh: 习惯是怎么形成的？

sents.en: In the book Atomic Habits, James Clear describes a four-step process by which habits are made.
sents.zh: 詹姆斯·克利尔在《掌控习惯》一书中，描述了习惯形成的四个步骤。

sents.en: These steps are cue, craving, response, and reward.
sents.zh: 这四步是：提示、渴望、反应和奖励。

sents.en: The cue tells your brain to begin a behavior.
sents.zh: 提示告诉大脑开始某个行为。

sents.en: The craving is what makes you want to do something.
sents.zh: 渴望是让你想去做某件事的动力。

sents.en: The response is the actual habit that you perform.
sents.zh: 反应就是你实际做出的那个习惯行为。

sents.en: The response, in turn, gives you a reward.
sents.zh: 而反应又会给你带来奖励。

sents.en: “Rewards are the end goal of every habit,” Clear writes.
sents.zh: 克利尔写道：“奖励是每个习惯的最终目标。”

sents.en: Consider this example.
sents.zh: 看看这个例子。

sents.en: Maybe you have the habit of often checking social media.
sents.zh: 也许你有经常刷社交媒体的习惯。

sents.en: The cue might be a feeling of boredom while you are near your computer or phone.
sents.zh: 提示可能是你在电脑或手机旁边时感到无聊。

sents.en: The craving could be a desire to stop that feeling.
sents.zh: 渴望可能是想摆脱这种感觉。

sents.en: The response is checking social media, and the reward is seeing something interesting.
sents.zh: 反应就是去刷社交媒体，奖励则是看到有意思的东西。

sents.en: When that process is repeated many times, it becomes a habit.
sents.zh: 这个过程重复很多次，就成了习惯。

sents.en: Clear believes that to create a good habit, you need to follow several steps.
sents.zh: 克利尔认为，要养成好习惯，需要遵循几个步骤。

sents.en: You need to make your new habit obvious, or easy to see or understand.
sents.zh: 你要让新习惯显而易见，也就是容易看到、容易理解。

sents.en: The habit should also be attractive, simple and satisfying.
sents.zh: 这个习惯还应该有吸引力、简单、让人满足。

sents.en: Let’s think about how you might develop an English study habit.
sents.zh: 我们来想想怎样养成学英语的习惯。

sents.en: You should organize your surroundings in such a way that the cues of your new habit are very obvious.
sents.zh: 你应该布置好周围的环境，让新习惯的提示非常明显。

sents.en: For example, if you want to get in the habit of studying English every day, leave English books or notes in a very clear place.
sents.zh: 比如，如果你想养成每天学英语的习惯，就把英语书或笔记放在非常显眼的地方。

sents.en: To make your habit attractive, Clear recommends joining a culture where your new desired behavior is the normal behavior.
sents.zh: 为了让习惯有吸引力，克利尔建议加入一种文化：在那里，你想养成的行为就是常态。

sents.en: For example, you could join a group of other English learners in online meetings.
sents.zh: 比如，你可以加入其他英语学习者的线上聚会。

sents.en: To make your new habit easy, you could decrease the number of steps you have to take in order to study.
sents.zh: 为了让新习惯简单易行，你可以减少开始学习前需要做的步骤。

sents.en: You could also try reducing the amount of time you study.
sents.zh: 也可以试着缩短学习时间。

sents.en: Clear suggests beginning your habits with limited, shorter time periods – two minutes for example.
sents.zh: 克利尔建议，一开始只花有限的、较短的时间来培养习惯——比如两分钟。

sents.en: As you repeat the practice over time, you can go longer.
sents.zh: 随着时间推移不断重复，你就可以学得更久。

sents.en: An important point to keep in mind is that if you place too many demands on yourself, you are more likely to give up on your new habit.
sents.zh: 要记住很重要的一点：如果你对自己要求太多，就更容易放弃新习惯。

sents.en: Finally, you need to make your habit satisfying.
sents.zh: 最后，你需要让习惯带来满足感。

sents.en: You can give yourself a reward after completing your new habit.
sents.zh: 完成新习惯后，你可以给自己一点奖励。

sents.en: For example, if you study English for 15 minutes, you could reward yourself by listening to a song you like.
sents.zh: 比如，学了 15 分钟英语后，你可以听一首喜欢的歌作为奖励。

sents.en: Or you could think about how much progress you have made since you first started studying English.
sents.zh: 或者想想自从开始学英语以来，你进步了多少。

sents.en: Wood notes that your reward should come right after you do your new habit.
sents.zh: 伍德指出，奖励应该在做完新习惯之后马上到来。

sents.en: “Rewards have to be experienced right after we do something in order to build habit associations... in memory,” she writes.
sents.zh: 她写道：“必须在做完某件事之后立刻体验到奖励，才能在记忆中建立起习惯的关联。”

sents.en: Building new habits can take time.
sents.zh: 养成新习惯可能需要时间。

sents.en: You may have to repeat an action many times before it becomes a habit.
sents.zh: 一个动作可能要重复很多次才会变成习惯。

sents.en: But with time, careful planning and continued practice, you can do it.
sents.zh: 但只要有时间、有周密的计划、坚持练习，你就能做到。

sents.en: I'm John Russell.
sents.zh: 我是约翰·拉塞尔。

items.title: Avoid Ineffective Study Methods
items.titleZh: 别再用低效的学习方法
items.series: Education Tips 学习技巧
items.summaryZh: 重读和划重点会让你产生“已经会了”的错觉。更好的方法是自我测试和间隔练习。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: John Russell wrote this story for Learning English. George Grow was the editor.

sents.en: Imagine you have a test in school.
sents.zh: 想象一下，你在学校有一场考试。

sents.en: It could be for a class in history or mathematics.
sents.zh: 可能是历史课或数学课的考试。

sents.en: Even worse, you could have an English test.
sents.zh: 更糟的是，可能是英语考试。

sents.en: How should you prepare for this terrible event?
sents.zh: 你该怎样为这件可怕的事做准备？

sents.en: What can you do before the big day to help you do better?
sents.zh: 在考试那天到来之前，你能做些什么让自己考得更好？

sents.en: Should you reread your history or math books?
sents.zh: 要不要把历史书或数学书再读一遍？

sents.en: What about underlining important words or sentences?
sents.zh: 在重要的词句下面画线又怎么样？

sents.en: If you are like many students, you probably use both rereading and underlining.
sents.zh: 如果你和很多学生一样，你大概两种方法都用过。

sents.en: But are these truly the best methods?
sents.zh: 可这些真的是最好的方法吗？

sents.en: Today, on our Education Report, we will explore effective and ineffective ways to study for tests.
sents.zh: 今天的《教育报道》，我们来探讨备考时哪些学习方法有效、哪些无效。

sents.en: You might learn that some study habits you used in the past might not be the best methods.
sents.zh: 你可能会发现，你过去的一些学习习惯未必是最好的方法。

sents.en: Are rereading and highlighting effective?
sents.zh: 重读和划重点有效吗？

sents.en: Rereading and highlighting are common strategies that you will see in schools around the world.
sents.zh: 重读和划重点是世界各地学校里都很常见的方法。

sents.en: Students look at information they have already read in an effort to remember what is important.
sents.zh: 学生把已经读过的内容再看一遍，想记住其中的重点。

sents.en: Students often combine rereading with highlighting.
sents.zh: 学生常常一边重读一边划重点。

sents.en: They underline important information in what they read with a writing instrument such as a marker.
sents.zh: 他们用记号笔之类的笔，把读到的重要信息画出来。

sents.en: American Mary Pyc is a cognitive scientist.
sents.zh: 美国人玛丽·皮克是一位认知科学家。

sents.en: She studies the human mind and its processes.
sents.zh: 她研究人类的心智及其运作过程。

sents.en: Pyc says that both rereading and highlighting are ineffective study tools.
sents.zh: 皮克说，重读和划重点都是效果不好的学习方法。

sents.en: While better than not studying at all, she believes they are not as useful as other habits.
sents.zh: 她认为，这比完全不学要好，但不如其他学习习惯有用。

sents.en: "For example, with rereading, it's maybe not as effective because you are not trying to actively retrieve the information.
sents.zh: “比如重读，它可能没那么有效，因为你并没有主动去提取信息。

sents.en: You are not seeing "what do I actually know about what I read?"
sents.zh: 你没有去检验‘我读过的内容，我到底掌握了多少？’

sents.en: With rereading what is going to happen is that it is going to feel like you already know the information because you've already read it.
sents.zh: 重读的结果是，你会觉得自己已经掌握了这些内容，因为你已经读过了。

sents.en: So, you have this sense of fluency that is leading you to think "Ok, yes, I know the information."
sents.zh: 于是你有一种很熟的感觉，让你以为‘好，没问题，这些我都会了’。”

sents.en: The problem with highlighting, Pyc says, is that students have a false sense of understanding - similar to when they reread information.
sents.zh: 皮克说，划重点的问题在于，学生会产生一种虚假的“懂了”的感觉——和重读时很像。

sents.en: Also, there is a second problem that comes with highlighting.
sents.zh: 而且，划重点还有第二个问题。

sents.en: "Students aren't always aware of what the most important information is.
sents.zh: “学生并不总是清楚什么才是最重要的信息。

sents.en: So it's possible that they are maybe highlighting details that aren't as important as the higher level concepts."
sents.zh: 所以他们画出来的可能是一些细节，而这些细节没有更高层次的概念重要。”

sents.en: What can you do?
sents.zh: 那该怎么办？

sents.en: So what should you do if rereading and highlighting are not the best ways to study for a test?
sents.zh: 既然重读和划重点不是备考的最佳方法，那该怎么做？

sents.en: One idea is to test yourself.
sents.zh: 一个办法是自我测试。

sents.en: We have discussed self-testing strategies in other education stories.
sents.zh: 我们在其他教育报道里讨论过自我测试的方法。

sents.en: Simple flashcards and practice exams can help when you want to make sure that you have learned something.
sents.zh: 想确认自己是否真的学会了，简单的抽认卡和模拟考试都会有帮助。

sents.en: Another strategy is what education experts have called “spaced practice.”
sents.zh: 另一个方法是教育专家所说的“间隔练习”。

sents.en: This means to practice remembering the new information over time, instead of doing everything all at once.
sents.zh: 意思是在一段时间里分多次练习回忆新内容，而不是一次全部做完。

sents.en: We will discuss spaced practice in a future Education Tips story.
sents.zh: 我们会在以后的《学习技巧》里专门讨论间隔练习。

sents.en: Regardless of which strategy you chose, you should know that effective learning takes time and it takes effort.
sents.zh: 不管你选择哪种方法，都要知道，有效的学习需要时间，也需要努力。

sents.en: The next time you have a test coming, try to plan for the big day so that you can give yourself time to engage in different study habits.
sents.zh: 下次快考试时，试着提前为那一天做好计划，给自己留出时间，用不同的学习方法。

sents.en: And remember, rereading and highlighting are better than not studying at all, but there are better methods out there!
sents.zh: 记住，重读和划重点总比完全不学好，但还有更好的方法！

sents.en: I'm John Russell.
sents.zh: 我是约翰·拉塞尔。

items.title: Sometimes Help Is Just 'A Phone Call Away'
items.series: Words and Their Stories 词汇典故
items.summaryZh: just a phone call away、blow up my phone、hold the phone、phone tag、phone it in 都是什么意思？
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Anna Matteo wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English.

sents.en: And now, Words and Their Stories, from VOA Learning English.
sents.zh: 下面是 VOA 慢速英语的《词汇典故》。

sents.en: On today’s show we talk about some expressions that deal with an important device in our lives – our phones.
sents.zh: 今天的节目，我们来聊几个和我们生活中一个重要设备——手机——有关的说法。

sents.en: With a smartphone, we can connect to the world.
sents.zh: 有了智能手机，我们就能和世界连接。

sents.en: In fact, we can say smartphones give us the world at our fingertips.
sents.zh: 其实可以说，智能手机让整个世界都在我们的指尖。

sents.en: Needless to say, we use phones to stay in contact with the people in our lives.
sents.zh: 不用说，我们用手机和生活中的人保持联系。

sents.en: We use them to reach out to our friends, family, neighbors, and co-workers.
sents.zh: 我们用手机联系朋友、家人、邻居和同事。

sents.en: So, when we tell someone that we are just a phone call away, what we are really telling them is that we are available.
sents.zh: 所以，当我们对某人说 we are just a phone call away（有事打个电话就行），我们真正想说的是：我随时都在。

sents.en: We are there for them.
sents.zh: 我们会支持他们。

sents.en: We often use this expression to offer help to someone who is in a difficult situation or just in need of a friendly voice.
sents.zh: 这个说法常常用来向处境困难、或者只是想听到一个友好声音的人提供帮助。

sents.en: For example, let’s say my friend is having a hard time with an advanced English course.
sents.zh: 比如，我的一个朋友在一门高级英语课上很吃力。

sents.en: The assignments are difficult, the material is hard to understand, and his teacher has not been answering his emails.
sents.zh: 作业很难，内容难懂，他的老师也一直没回他的邮件。

sents.en: I can say to him, “Look, if you ever need help, I’m just a phone call away.
sents.zh: 我可以对他说：“听着，要是需要帮忙，打个电话就行。

sents.en: Call anytime!”
sents.zh: 随时都可以打！”

sents.en: It’s good to be available to some people some of the time.
sents.zh: 对某些人来说，有时候随叫随到是件好事。

sents.en: But maybe not all the time.
sents.zh: 但也许不是一直都这样。

sents.en: We all have someone in our lives who contacts us too much.
sents.zh: 我们每个人生活中都有那么一个联系我们太频繁的人。

sents.en: They may blow up our phones with a flood of calls and text messages.
sents.zh: 他们可能用一大堆电话和短信把我们的手机“打爆”（blow up our phones）。

sents.en: When your phone blows up, someone is trying to contact you repeatedly.
sents.zh: 手机被打爆，就是有人一遍又一遍地想联系你。

sents.en: Here's an example.
sents.zh: 举个例子。

sents.en: Let’s say your neighbor, Jana, is having trouble with another neighbor, Jake.
sents.zh: 假设你的邻居贾娜和另一个邻居杰克闹了矛盾。

sents.en: And you are in the middle of it.
sents.zh: 而你夹在中间。

sents.en: They are both blowing up your phone with calls and texts about their disagreement.
sents.zh: 他们俩都为这事用电话和短信把你的手机打爆了。

sents.en: You can tell them, “Hold the phone!
sents.zh: 你可以对他们说：“Hold the phone（等一下）！

sents.en: Just stop!
sents.zh: 停！

sents.en: Talk to each other and work out your problems because I’ve had enough.”
sents.zh: 你们俩自己谈谈，把问题解决掉，我受够了。”

sents.en: The expression hold the phone is a way to say “wait” or “stop.”
sents.zh: hold the phone 的意思是“等等”或“停下”。

sents.en: We use it when we hear something surprising or when we have had enough of a situation.
sents.zh: 听到让人意外的事，或者对某种情况受够了的时候，我们会这么说。

sents.en: And it doesn’t have to be about phone calls or texts.
sents.zh: 而且它不一定和打电话、发短信有关。

sents.en: For example, let’s say a friend tells me that my favorite singer is coming to town.
sents.zh: 比如，一个朋友告诉我，我最喜欢的歌手要来我们城市了。

sents.en: I can’t believe it!
sents.zh: 我简直不敢相信！

sents.en: So, I can say, “Hold the phone!
sents.zh: 于是我可以说：“Hold the phone！

sents.en: Are you serious?”
sents.zh: 你是认真的吗？”

sents.en: It's like saying, "Hold on a minute!"
sents.zh: 就像在说“等一下！”

sents.en: Now, let’s go back to your arguing neighbors, Jana and Jake.
sents.zh: 现在，我们回到你那两位吵架的邻居贾娜和杰克。

sents.en: Let’s say they take your advice.
sents.zh: 假设他们听了你的建议。

sents.en: They are willing to work out their problems.
sents.zh: 他们愿意把问题解决掉。

sents.en: They try to call each other but the keep missing each other’s calls.
sents.zh: 他们给对方打电话，可总是错过对方的来电。

sents.en: First Jana calls Jake, but he isn’t available.
sents.zh: 先是贾娜给杰克打电话，可他没空。

sents.en: Then Jake calls her back, but now Jana isn’t available.
sents.zh: 然后杰克回电话，可这回贾娜又没空。

sents.en: They play phone tag like this for days until they finally speak to each other.
sents.zh: 他们就这样“电话捉迷藏”（phone tag）好几天，最后才终于通上话。

sents.en: Tag is a child’s game.
sents.zh: tag 是一种小孩玩的游戏。

sents.en: One person is “it” and must chase and tag, or touch, the other children.
sents.zh: 一个人当“鬼”，要去追其他孩子，碰到谁就算抓到。

sents.en: So, phone tag is when two people try to contact each other but their calls go unanswered.
sents.zh: 所以 phone tag 就是两个人都想联系对方，可电话总是没人接。

sents.en: At least Jake and Jana are trying to work out their problems.
sents.zh: 至少杰克和贾娜在努力解决问题。

sents.en: When it comes to keeping relationships happy in the neighborhood, they are not phoning it in.
sents.zh: 在维护邻里关系这件事上，他们没有敷衍了事（phoning it in）。

sents.en: When we phone it in, we don’t try our best at something.
sents.zh: phone it in 的意思是做事不尽全力。

sents.en: We don’t give our best efforts.
sents.zh: 不拿出最大的努力。

sents.en: For example, some people who lose interest in their jobs might start phoning it in.
sents.zh: 比如，有些人对工作失去兴趣后，可能就开始敷衍了事。

sents.en: They stop trying and do not do their best work.
sents.zh: 他们不再努力，也不再拿出最好的状态工作。

sents.en: That's not the case with us here at VOA Learning English. we are not phoning it in.
sents.zh: 我们 VOA 慢速英语可不是这样，我们没有敷衍了事。

sents.en: We work hard every day to bring you new learning English content.
sents.zh: 我们每天都在努力，为你带来新的英语学习内容。

sents.en: And that’s all the time we have for this Words and Their Stories.
sents.zh: 本期《词汇典故》就到这里。

sents.en: Until next time, I’m Anna Matteo.
sents.zh: 下次再见，我是安娜·马泰奥。

items.title: Sometimes We 'Spread Ourself Too Thin'
items.series: Words and Their Stories 词汇典故
items.summaryZh: spread yourself too thin 和 bite off more than you can chew：揽的事太多，结果哪件都做不好。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Anna Matteo wrote this story for VOA Learning English.

sents.en: And now, Words and Their Stories, from VOA Learning English.
sents.zh: 下面是 VOA 慢速英语的《词汇典故》。

sents.en: Today we talk about our busy lives.
sents.zh: 今天我们来聊聊忙碌的生活。

sents.en: Many people have family and work responsibilities.
sents.zh: 很多人既要顾家，又要工作。

sents.en: We might have religious or community activities.
sents.zh: 我们可能还有宗教活动或社区活动。

sents.en: Taking care of our health is also important.
sents.zh: 照顾好自己的健康也很重要。

sents.en: And let’s not forget about our personal projects, our interests, and our friendships.
sents.zh: 还别忘了我们自己的项目、兴趣爱好和朋友。

sents.en: With everything on our plate, it is easy to feel overwhelmed, overextended, and overcommitted.
sents.zh: 事情一多，就很容易觉得招架不住、分身乏术、答应得太多。

sents.en: However, if we try to do too much, we may spread ourselves too thin.
sents.zh: 可是，如果我们想做的事太多，就可能 spread ourselves too thin（精力分散得太薄）。

sents.en: This expression means we have taken on too much.
sents.zh: 这个说法的意思是我们揽的事太多了。

sents.en: We are pushed to the limit.
sents.zh: 我们已经被逼到极限了。

sents.en: People who are spread too thin, take on too many jobs, projects, or goals.
sents.zh: 精力分散得太薄的人，会同时接下太多工作、项目或目标。

sents.en: The heavy load requires more energy or attention than they possess.
sents.zh: 这么重的负担，需要的精力或注意力超过了他们所拥有的。

sents.en: If we work on many projects simultaneously, or at the same time, it is possible that none will get done well, if they get done at all.
sents.zh: 如果我们同时做很多个项目，很可能哪个都做不好，甚至一个都做不完。

sents.en: And it is possible such multitasking could stress us out.
sents.zh: 而且这样同时干好几件事，还可能让我们压力很大。

sents.en: Being spread too thin can also be described as biting off more than we can chew.
sents.zh: 精力分散得太薄，也可以说是 bite off more than we can chew（贪多嚼不烂）。

sents.en: When we bite off more than we can chew, we attempt to do more than is possible.
sents.zh: 当我们“贪多嚼不烂”时，就是想做超出能力范围的事。

sents.en: Now, let’s hear these some of these terms and expressions used in a conversation.
sents.zh: 下面，我们来听听这些词语和说法在对话里怎么用。

sents.en: So, how are your classes going?
sents.zh: 你的课上得怎么样？

sents.en: Not great.
sents.zh: 不太好。

sents.en: Many of my best students are failing my course.
sents.zh: 我好几个最好的学生这门课都快不及格了。

sents.en: They all missed an important deadline for a project.
sents.zh: 他们都错过了一个项目的重要截止日期。

sents.en: That's strange.
sents.zh: 奇怪了。

sents.en: What else do they have going on?
sents.zh: 他们还在忙别的什么事吗？

sents.en: A lot!
sents.zh: 多着呢！

sents.en: They are all performing in the same play.
sents.zh: 他们都在演同一部戏。

sents.en: So, they have had rehearsals every night for the past month.
sents.zh: 所以过去一个月每天晚上都在排练。

sents.en: And many have part-time jobs as well.
sents.zh: 而且很多人还在打零工。

sents.en: Sounds like they’ve spread themselves too thin.
sents.zh: 听起来他们是把自己的精力摊得太薄了。

sents.en: They’ve got too much going on.
sents.zh: 手上的事太多了。

sents.en: I think you’re right.
sents.zh: 我觉得你说得对。

sents.en: So, what are you going to do?
sents.zh: 那你打算怎么办？

sents.en: Well, first I’ll extend the deadline.
sents.zh: 嗯，我先把截止日期往后延。

sents.en: And then I’m going to warn them about biting off more than they can chew.
sents.zh: 然后提醒他们别贪多嚼不烂。

sents.en: And that’s all the time we have for this Words and Their Stories.
sents.zh: 本期《词汇典故》就到这里。

sents.en: Until next time, I’m Anna Matteo.
sents.zh: 下次再见，我是安娜·马泰奥。

items.title: Thomas Edison: Inventor and Busy Team Leader
items.titleZh: 爱迪生：发明家和忙碌的团队领导
items.series: Science & Technology / People in America
items.summaryZh: 爱迪生自学成才，带领团队每年申请上百项专利，发明了电灯、留声机和电影胶片。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Paul Thompson reported this story for VOA’s People in America program. Jill Robbins adapted it for Learning English.

sents.en: The inventor Thomas Alva Edison had a major effect on the lives of people around the world.
sents.zh: 发明家托马斯·阿尔瓦·爱迪生对全世界人们的生活产生了重大影响。

sents.en: Thomas Edison is remembered most for the electric light, his phonograph, and his work with motion pictures.
sents.zh: 人们记住托马斯·爱迪生，主要是因为电灯、留声机，以及他在电影方面的工作。

sents.en: Edison was born on February 11, 1847, in Milan, Ohio.
sents.zh: 爱迪生 1847 年 2 月 11 日出生在俄亥俄州的米兰。

sents.en: He was mostly self-taught.
sents.zh: 他基本上是自学成才的。

sents.en: His mother taught him reading, writing, and mathematics.
sents.zh: 他的母亲教他读书、写字和算术。

sents.en: He learned from books, and he experimented.
sents.zh: 他从书本中学习，也动手做实验。

sents.en: At the age of 10, he experimented with chemicals and electricity.
sents.zh: 10 岁时，他就开始做化学和电的实验。

sents.en: He built a telegraph machine and, at the age of 16, he went to work as a telegraph operator.
sents.zh: 他造了一台电报机，16 岁时去当了电报员。

sents.en: He continued his work with electricity, making improved telegraph machines, and he invented an electrical voting machine.
sents.zh: 他继续研究电，改进电报机，还发明了一台电动投票机。

sents.en: Edison earned enough money from his early inventions to start his own company in 1871.
sents.zh: 爱迪生靠早期的发明赚了足够的钱，1871 年创办了自己的公司。

sents.en: Instead of working alone, he worked with a group of employees on many different projects at one time.
sents.zh: 他不是单打独斗，而是同时和一群员工一起做很多不同的项目。

sents.en: They asked the United States government for patents to protect more than one hundred devices or inventions each year.
sents.zh: 他们每年为一百多项装置或发明向美国政府申请专利保护。

sents.en: He was an extremely busy man.
sents.zh: 他是个极其忙碌的人。

sents.en: In 1913, a popular magazine at the time called Thomas Edison the most useful man in America.
sents.zh: 1913 年，当时一本很受欢迎的杂志称托马斯·爱迪生是“美国最有用的人”。

sents.en: He almost never slept more than four or five hours a night.
sents.zh: 他每晚几乎从不睡超过四五个小时。

sents.en: He usually worked 18 hours each day because he enjoyed what he was doing.
sents.zh: 他通常每天工作 18 个小时，因为他喜欢自己在做的事。

sents.en: A reporter asked Edison in 1917 which of his many inventions he enjoyed the most.
sents.zh: 1917 年，一位记者问爱迪生，他那么多发明里最喜欢哪一个。

sents.en: He answered, the phonograph was really the most interesting.
sents.zh: 他回答说，留声机确实是最有意思的。

sents.en: The hardest invention to develop, he said, was the electric light.
sents.zh: 他说，最难研制的发明是电灯。

sents.en: He said that it was the most difficult and the most important.
sents.zh: 他说电灯是最难的，也是最重要的。

sents.en: He also invented the modern motion picture film.
sents.zh: 他还发明了现代电影胶片。

sents.en: In 1928, he received a special medal of honor from the Congress of the United States.
sents.zh: 1928 年，他获得了美国国会颁发的一枚特别荣誉奖章。

sents.en: Thomas Edison died on January 6, 1931.
sents.zh: 托马斯·爱迪生于 1931 年 1 月 6 日去世。

sents.en: People worldwide have had easier and more enjoyable lives because of his inventions.
sents.zh: 因为他的发明，全世界的人们生活得更轻松、更有乐趣。

sents.en: I’m John Russell.
sents.zh: 我是约翰·拉塞尔。

items.title: Wilbur and Orville Wright: The First Airplane
items.titleZh: 莱特兄弟和第一架飞机
items.series: Science & Technology / People in America
items.summaryZh: 1903 年 12 月 17 日，莱特兄弟在北卡罗来纳完成了人类第一次动力飞行，飞了 12 秒、36 米。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Marilyn Rice Christiano wrote this story for VOA Learning English. John Russell adapted it.

sents.en: Wilbur and Orville Wright are the American inventors who made a small engine-powered flying machine.
sents.zh: 威尔伯·莱特和奥维尔·莱特是美国发明家，他们造出了一架靠小型发动机驱动的飞行器。

sents.en: They proved that flight without the aid of gas-filled balloons was possible.
sents.zh: 他们证明了不靠充气气球也能飞上天。

sents.en: Wilbur Wright was born in 1867 near Melville, Indiana.
sents.zh: 威尔伯·莱特 1867 年出生在印第安纳州米尔维尔附近。

sents.en: His brother Orville was born four years later in Dayton, Ohio.
sents.zh: 他的弟弟奥维尔四年后出生在俄亥俄州的代顿。

sents.en: As they grew up, the Wright brothers experimented with mechanical things.
sents.zh: 兄弟俩从小就爱摆弄各种机械。

sents.en: Later, the Wright brothers began to design their own flying machine.
sents.zh: 后来，莱特兄弟开始设计自己的飞行器。

sents.en: They used ideas they had developed from earlier experiments with a toy helicopter, kites, the printing machine and bicycles.
sents.zh: 他们用上了以前玩玩具直升机、风筝、印刷机和自行车时琢磨出来的点子。

sents.en: Soon, they needed a place to test their ideas about flight.
sents.zh: 很快，他们需要一个地方来验证自己关于飞行的想法。

sents.en: The best place with the best wind conditions seemed to be a piece of sandy land in North Carolina along the coast of the Atlantic Ocean.
sents.zh: 风力条件最好的地方，似乎是北卡罗来纳州大西洋沿岸的一片沙地。

sents.en: It was called Kill Devil Hill, near the town of Kitty Hawk.
sents.zh: 那地方叫斩魔山，在基蒂霍克镇附近。

sents.en: The Wright brothers did many tests with gliders at Kitty Hawk.
sents.zh: 莱特兄弟在基蒂霍克用滑翔机做了很多次试验。

sents.en: With these tests, they learned how to solve many problems.
sents.zh: 通过这些试验，他们学会了解决很多问题。

sents.en: By the autumn of 1903, Wilbur and Orville had designed and built an airplane powered by a gasoline engine.
sents.zh: 到 1903 年秋天，威尔伯和奥维尔已经设计并造出了一架由汽油发动机驱动的飞机。

sents.en: The plane had wings 12 meters across.
sents.zh: 这架飞机的翼展有 12 米。

sents.en: It weighed about 340 kilograms, including the pilot.
sents.zh: 连同驾驶员在内，它重约 340 公斤。

sents.en: On December 17th, 1903, they made the world's first flight in a machine that was heavier than air and powered by an engine.
sents.zh: 1903 年 12 月 17 日，他们完成了世界上第一次比空气重、由发动机驱动的飞行器的飞行。

sents.en: Orville flew the plane 36 meters.
sents.zh: 奥维尔驾驶飞机飞了 36 米。

sents.en: He was in the air for 12 seconds.
sents.zh: 他在空中停留了 12 秒。

sents.en: The two brothers made three more flights that day.
sents.zh: 那天兄弟俩又飞了三次。

sents.en: Four other men watched the Wright brothers' first flights.
sents.zh: 另外有四个人观看了莱特兄弟的首次飞行。

sents.en: One of the men took pictures.
sents.zh: 其中一人拍了照片。

sents.en: Few newspapers, however, noted the event.
sents.zh: 然而，几乎没有报纸报道这件事。

sents.en: It was almost five years before the Wright brothers became famous.
sents.zh: 差不多过了五年，莱特兄弟才出名。

sents.en: In 1908, Wilbur went to France.
sents.zh: 1908 年，威尔伯去了法国。

sents.en: He gave demonstration flights at heights of 90 meters.
sents.zh: 他在 90 米的高度做了飞行表演。

sents.en: A French company agreed to begin making the Wright brothers' flying machine.
sents.zh: 一家法国公司同意开始制造莱特兄弟的飞行器。

sents.en: Orville made successful flights in the United States at the time Wilbur was in France.
sents.zh: 威尔伯在法国的同时，奥维尔在美国也成功完成了几次飞行。

sents.en: The United States War Department agreed to buy a Wright brothers' plane.
sents.zh: 美国陆军部同意购买一架莱特兄弟的飞机。

sents.en: Wilbur and Orville suddenly became world heroes.
sents.zh: 威尔伯和奥维尔一下子成了世界英雄。

sents.en: But the brothers were not seeking fame.
sents.zh: 可兄弟俩并不追求名气。

sents.en: They returned to Dayton where they continued to improve their airplanes.
sents.zh: 他们回到代顿，继续改进他们的飞机。

sents.en: They taught many others how to fly.
sents.zh: 他们还教会了很多人飞行。

sents.en: Wilbur Wright died of typhoid fever in 1912.
sents.zh: 威尔伯·莱特 1912 年死于伤寒。

sents.en: Orville Wright continued designing and inventing until he died many years later, in 1948.
sents.zh: 奥维尔·莱特一直坚持设计和发明，直到很多年后的 1948 年去世。

sents.en: Today, the Wright brothers' first airplane is in the Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Visitors to the museum can look at the Wright brothers' small plane.
sents.zh: 如今，莱特兄弟的第一架飞机陈列在华盛顿的航空航天博物馆里。参观者可以在那里看到莱特兄弟的小飞机。

sents.en: Then they can walk to another area and see space vehicles and a rock collected from the moon.
sents.zh: 然后再走到另一个展区，看看航天器和从月球上采回来的岩石。

sents.en: The world has changed a lot since Wilbur and Orville Wright began the modern age of flight over one hundred years ago.
sents.zh: 自从一百多年前威尔伯和奥维尔·莱特开启现代航空时代以来，世界已经发生了巨大的变化。

sents.en: I’m John Russell.
sents.zh: 我是约翰·拉塞尔。

items.title: Can Bees, Dogs Identify Cancer Earlier Than Machines?
items.titleZh: 蜜蜂和狗能比机器更早发现癌症吗？
items.series: Health & Lifestyle 健康与生活
items.summaryZh: 蜜蜂能从呼吸中闻出肺癌，准确率 93%；狗的嗅觉比人灵敏一万到十万倍，科学家希望造出同样灵敏的机器。
items.license: 公有领域（VOA 自制内容，美国政府作品）
items.credit: Dora Mekouar reported this story for VOA News. Jill Robbins adapted it for Learning English.

sents.en: Researchers at Michigan State University recently found that bees’ sense of “smell” is sensitive enough to identify chemical smells of cancer.
sents.zh: 密歇根州立大学的研究人员最近发现，蜜蜂的“嗅觉”灵敏到足以识别癌症的化学气味。

sents.en: Bees sense chemicals in their environment using antennae, structures on their heads, which serve as “noses” to sense smells.
sents.zh: 蜜蜂用触角感知环境中的化学物质，触角长在头上，相当于用来闻气味的“鼻子”。

sents.en: The researchers wrote in a study published last month that honeybees can sniff out lung cancer on a patient’s breath.
sents.zh: 研究人员在上个月发表的一项研究中写道，蜜蜂能从病人的呼吸中闻出肺癌。

sents.en: Debajit Saha is an assistant professor of biomedical engineering at Michigan State University.
sents.zh: 德巴吉特·萨哈是密歇根州立大学生物医学工程助理教授。

sents.en: He was part of a team that published the research.
sents.zh: 他是发表这项研究的团队成员之一。

sents.en: “Our world is visual. [The] insects’ world is all based on smell, so their sense of smell is very, very good,” Saha said.
sents.zh: 萨哈说：“我们的世界以视觉为主。昆虫的世界则完全建立在气味上，所以它们的嗅觉非常非常好。”

sents.en: “There is quite a bit of research that shows that when some cancer grows inside our body, our breath actually changes.
sents.zh: “有不少研究表明，当某种癌症在我们体内生长时，我们的呼吸其实会发生变化。

sents.en: Our research does show that honeybees can detect lung cancer and possibly other diseases based on the smell of those cells.”
sents.zh: 我们的研究确实表明，蜜蜂能根据这些细胞的气味发现肺癌，可能还有其他疾病。”

sents.en: Saha and his team placed bees in small harnesses and attached small wires to their brains.
sents.zh: 萨哈和团队给蜜蜂套上小小的固定带，并在它们的大脑上接了细小的电线。

sents.en: The insects were then placed near chemicals that are like the breath of a person with lung cancer.
sents.zh: 然后把这些蜜蜂放在一些化学物质旁边，这些物质的气味类似肺癌病人的呼吸。

sents.en: The scientists said that the bees could tell the difference between the cancer breath and the laboratory copy of the healthy human breath 93 percent of the time.
sents.zh: 科学家说，蜜蜂区分“癌症呼吸”和实验室仿制的健康人呼吸，准确率达到 93%。

sents.en: The scientists added that the bees could also tell the difference between different kinds of lung cancer.
sents.zh: 科学家还说，蜜蜂还能区分不同类型的肺癌。

sents.en: The discovery could help doctors detect many cancers, including lung, breast, head and neck, and colorectal cancers, earlier than other methods.
sents.zh: 这项发现或许能帮助医生比用其他方法更早地发现多种癌症，包括肺癌、乳腺癌、头颈癌和结直肠癌。

sents.en: Saha says detecting cancers this way would be an improvement.
sents.zh: 萨哈说，用这种方式检测癌症会是一大进步。

sents.en: “The reason is, many times we detect the cancer late,” when a growth has become too big to control easily.
sents.zh: “原因在于，很多时候我们发现癌症时已经太晚了”，那时肿瘤已经大到很难控制。

sents.en: But, he added, when cancer starts growing the breath starts changing much earlier.
sents.zh: 不过他补充说，癌症开始生长时，呼吸早早就开始变化了。

sents.en: He hopes to develop a system that a patient will be able to breathe into and which can be carried around easily.
sents.zh: 他希望开发一套病人对着吹气就能检测、又便于携带的系统。

sents.en: This would deliver test results immediately.
sents.zh: 这样就能立刻拿到检测结果。

sents.en: “Hopefully, within the next five years, we'll have something to show that humans can be diagnosed using these insect brain disc sensors,” Saha said.
sents.zh: 萨哈说：“希望在未来五年内，我们能拿出成果，证明可以用这种昆虫大脑传感器来给人做诊断。”

sents.en: Using animals to detect cancer is not a new idea.
sents.zh: 用动物来检测癌症并不是什么新想法。

sents.en: At the Penn Vet Working Dog Center at the University of Pennsylvania, researchers are training dogs to smell some kinds of cancer.
sents.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚大学的宾大兽医工作犬中心，研究人员正在训练狗去闻出某些癌症。

sents.en: Cindy Otto is executive director of the Penn Vet Working Dog Center in Philadelphia.
sents.zh: 辛迪·奥托是费城宾大兽医工作犬中心的执行主任。

sents.en: She said many other animals also have very good senses of smell.
sents.zh: 她说，很多其他动物的嗅觉也非常好。

sents.en: “But part of what makes dogs so good is that they cooperate with humans, and so, they communicate that information,” she added.
sents.zh: 她补充说：“但狗之所以这么出色，部分原因是它们会和人合作，所以能把这些信息传达出来。”

sents.en: The dogs are in a program where they live with families and are brought to “work” each day.
sents.zh: 这些狗参加了一个项目，它们和寄养家庭住在一起，每天被带去“上班”。

sents.en: Not all dogs can do this work.
sents.zh: 不是所有的狗都能做这份工作。

sents.en: Otto said,
sents.zh: 奥托说：

sents.en: “They need to love it to be engaged.
sents.zh: “它们得真心喜欢，才会投入。

sents.en: And so, it's a really fun game for them.”
sents.zh: 所以这对它们来说是个非常好玩的游戏。”

sents.en: Some researchers say that dogs detect cancer better than machines.
sents.zh: 一些研究人员说，狗检测癌症比机器更准。

sents.en: They note that a dog’s sense of smell is 10,000 to 100,000 times sharper than that of humans.
sents.zh: 他们指出，狗的嗅觉比人灵敏一万到十万倍。

sents.en: Amritha Mallikarjun is another postdoctoral researcher at the center.
sents.zh: 阿姆丽塔·马利卡尔琼是该中心的另一位博士后研究员。

sents.en: She said dogs are more sensitive to smells than any machines sold today.
sents.zh: 她说，狗对气味的敏感程度超过目前市面上的任何机器。

sents.en: But the scientists hope to create a machine that will identify disease just as well as dogs.
sents.zh: 不过科学家们希望造出一台能像狗一样准确识别疾病的机器。

sents.en: Otto said doctors in ancient Greece and Rome used odor as a tool to identify disease.
sents.zh: 奥托说，古希腊和古罗马的医生就用气味作为识别疾病的手段。

sents.en: She hopes the researchers can build on that “and advance the health of not only humans, but dogs and other species as well.”
sents.zh: 她希望研究人员能在此基础上更进一步，“不仅促进人类的健康，也促进狗和其他物种的健康”。

sents.en: I’m Jill Robbins.
sents.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。
